epic.title: Orchestrator V3 — M0 vocabulary/layout freeze + M1 chat spine
epic.goal: Freeze the product vocabulary and on-disk layout decision (M0), then ship the interactive chat layer on the UN-refactored engine (M1): Ideas + Research usable daily as manual chats and watchable auto debates, with 'step in', 'let them discuss', fork, and honest lifecycle states — all before any deep engine refactor.

tasks.title: Layout decision doc — flat M1 chat naming, lock-collision rule, back-compat rule
tasks.goal: A written, reviewed decision that M1 chats live as FLAT legacy project dirs named `<project>--<section>--<chat-slug>`, that the nested layout `workspace/<project>/<section>/<chat-slug>/` is implemented only in task 3.0, plus the lock-name collision rule and the legacy back-compat rule.
tasks.context: Verified against code: engine discovery `find_apps` (orchestrator.py:6400–6421) is strictly flat — it lists direct children of the workspace root, skips dotfiles/.orchestrator/.git, and requires `<dir>/initial_prompt/initial_prompt.md`; nested dirs are ignored by design. GUI discovery is flat too (`BackgroundProjectLoader.discoverApps`, called at OrchestratorStore.swift:866) and locks are keyed by top-level dir name: `<root>/.orch-locks/<name>.lock` (OrchestratorStore.swift:3312 and the legacy `<engine>/locks/<name>.lock` at :3098). So a chat IS a flat project dir until 3.0. Trap discovered while verifying: `OrchestratorStore.slugify` (OrchestratorStore.swift:2980–2993) collapses consecutive dashes — `--` can never appear INSIDE a slugified component, which is exactly what makes `--` a safe separator, but it also means the flat name must be assembled by joining three already-slugified components with a literal `--`, never by slugifying the joined string (that would yield single dashes and break parsing). Because flat dir names are filesystem-unique at the root and lock name == dir name, lock uniqueness follows — document that chain explicitly. No drift from the plan found.
subtasks: Add a 'Layout (M1 interim)' section to GLOSSARY.md documenting: target nested layout `workspace/<project>/<section>/<chat-slug>/` (+ artifacts/, conductor/) is IMPLEMENTED in task 3.0, not before.

Document the flat naming convention `<project>--<section>--<chat-slug>`: each component independently slugified (OrchestratorStore.slugify semantics: lowercase ASCII alnum, single dashes, ≤40 chars, never consecutive dashes), then joined with literal `--`; parsing splits on `--` and is unambiguous because components cannot contain `--`.

Document the lock-collision rule: locks are `<root>/.orch-locks/<dir-name>.lock` (OrchestratorStore.swift:3312; engine legacy `locks/<name>.lock`); dir-name uniqueness at the flat root is what guarantees lock uniqueness, so chat minting MUST reject a name that already exists (suffix `-2`, `-3` … per the ChatHome.createRun precedent, ChatHome.swift:236–240).

Document the back-compat rule: any dir with `agent_state.json` at its root is a legacy single-chat project forever — 3.0's migration must never rewrite it into the nest without an explicit dry-run-diffed migration.
Document the discovery contract a minted chat dir must satisfy today: `initial_prompt/initial_prompt.md` present (find_apps, orchestrator.py:6420) plus `workflow.txt` naming the chat workflow.
Update orchestrator-v3-engineering-plan.md task 0.2 row status to point at the merged doc; submit for design review (the plan's gate).
acceptance_criteria: The doc states, with code citations, that find_apps (orchestrator.py:6400–6421) and GUI discovery + .orch-locks naming are flat today — and therefore M1 chats are flat dirs.
The naming convention specifies component-wise slugify THEN join with `--`, and explicitly forbids slugifying the joined string (with the collapse-consecutive-dashes rationale).
The lock-collision rule is derived, not asserted: dir-name uniqueness → lock-name uniqueness; mint-time uniqueness suffixing is specified.
The back-compat rule (`agent_state.json` at root = legacy single-chat project forever) is stated and marked binding on task 3.0.
The doc does NOT implement anything — zero code changes in this task.

tasks.title: `conversational` phase flag in workflow schema + process_phase
tasks.goal: A workflow phase can declare `conversational: true`; the engine then runs rounds as: drain human_inbox.txt → roster responds → wait for the next human message, with no coordinator/consensus/vote, ending on an explicit user command.
tasks.context: All plan anchors verified: process_phase at orchestrator.py:5270, its sequential round loop at 5515–5629 (drain_human_inbox called at 5529 at round open and 5629 before the coordinator turn), drain_human_inbox at 2592, _await_approval at 6342 (a 2s `poll` loop over approvals/<phase>.{ok,edit,changes} decision files — the poll to generalize into an inbox-wait helper). Agent turns reuse the `_discussion_turn` pattern (5541–5556): per-thread cfg copy, build_context, persona preamble, `call_agent_sessioned` with delta prompts (`_delta_discuss_prompt`, 1588). Phase schema lives in workflows.py `Phase` (__slots__ at 89–93, __init__ 95, to_json 141, from_json 154) — Phase.from_json DROPS unknown keys, so the field must be added there or chat workflow JSON silently loses it. Two traps found by reading code: (1) `_resume_round_state` (2540) counts a round complete only if a `**Coordinator (` block follows it — a conversational transcript has none, so the stock resume path would discard EVERY round; conversational resume must be append-only instead. (2) process_phase's return contract feeds consensus/final_output into the pipeline — the phase must complete honestly (user-ended), not fabricate a `CONSENSUS: YES` footer.
subtasks: workflows.py: add `conversational` to Phase.__slots__, __init__ (default False via _as_bool), to_json, and from_json; keep the legacy 4-tuple contract untouched.

orchestrator.py: extract `_await_inbox(app_dir, phase_key, state, timeout, poll=2.0)` generalizing _await_approval's decision-file poll (6342–6397): returns ('message', None) when human_inbox.txt is non-empty, ('end', None) when approvals/<phase_key>.ok appears, ('timeout', None) at deadline; sets/clears an honest waiting marker in state (e.g. state['awaiting_human'] = phase_key) with save_state, mirroring how _await_approval manages state['awaiting_approval'].

process_phase: when phasedef.get('conversational'): branch before the standard rounds_iter loop into a conversational loop — per round: append '### Round N' header, drain_human_inbox (2592), run every roster agent via the _discussion_turn pattern (parallel, roster-order append, PASS protocol and unavailable-agent skip notes preserved), then _await_inbox; on 'end' finalize, on 'message' next round, on 'timeout' finalize honestly with a 'conversation idle timeout' note.

Skip coordinator turn, consensus detection, quality gate, and forced vote entirely for conversational phases; final_output = the full conversational transcript; footer written WITHOUT a CONSENSUS/VOTE marker, with an explicit 'ENDED BY USER' (or 'IDLE TIMEOUT') line instead.

Crash resume: for conversational phases bypass _resume_round_state's coordinator heuristic — recover the transcript verbatim and resume append-only at the next round number (comment WHY next to the bypass, citing 2558–2566).
Emit events (evlib.emit_event) for round start and awaiting-human so the GUI can render the waiting state.

Tests: tests/test_conversational.py — stub call_agent/call_agent_sessioned; a writer thread drops inbox messages then approvals/<key>.ok; assert block order, no Coordinator block, state waiting flags set/cleared, phase completes; add a resume test (pre-seed a transcript, assert no rounds discarded).
Run the full suite (`make test-strict`) to prove existing workflows unchanged, then `make verify` on macOS.
acceptance_criteria: A phase with conversational:true runs: drain inbox → all roster agents respond (personas, delta prompts, PASS protocol intact) → block until next human message or end command.
No coordinator turn, consensus check, quality-gate repair, or forced vote executes for a conversational phase.
The phase ends when approvals/<phase_key>.ok appears; final_output is the transcript; the footer never contains a fabricated CONSENSUS: YES.

While waiting, agent_state.json shows an explicit awaiting-human marker that is cleared on wake and on phase end (never left stale after crash-resume re-entry, mirroring the 7208–7216 re-arm pattern).
Killing the engine mid-conversation and re-running resumes append-only: zero previously-recorded rounds are discarded (the _resume_round_state coordinator heuristic is provably bypassed).
A workflow WITHOUT the flag is byte-for-byte unaffected: full existing suite green.
Phase.from_json/to_json round-trips conversational:true; legacy JSON without the key loads with False.
Timeout does not hang forever and does not mark the phase failed — it finalizes with an honest idle-timeout note.
QA verifies via the scripted-inbox test: transcript contains human blocks ('**You (human) — …**') interleaved in send order.
test_plan: Gate (from plan): unit tests — conversational phase with scripted inbox; existing workflows unchanged (full suite).
tests/test_conversational.py: scripted-inbox happy path, end-command path, idle-timeout path, crash-resume append-only path, no-coordinator-block assertion.
Schema round-trip test in the existing workflows test file (Phase to_json/from_json with and without the flag).
`make verify` (test-strict + gui-build + gui-test + doctor) green before merge.

tasks.title: Event-driven inbox wake — 250ms mtime tick for conversational + approval waits
tasks.goal: Replace the fixed 2s sleep in the inbox/approval wait loops with a ~250ms tick that does only cheap stat checks, so a human message wakes the engine in well under a second without measurable CPU cost.
tasks.context: Verified: _await_approval (orchestrator.py:6342) sleeps `poll=2.0` between existence checks on three decision files; task 1.1 generalizes that loop into `_await_inbox`, which additionally watches human_inbox.txt. Today drain_human_inbox (2592) reads the whole inbox file every call; the wait loop must NOT do that every 250ms — instead os.stat the watched paths and only read on mtime/size change (mtime granularity on APFS is fine at 250ms, but compare (mtime_ns, size) tuples, not mtime seconds, to survive coarse-mtime filesystems and same-second rewrites). Approval decision files are checked by os.path.exists, already cheap — for them only the tick changes. Scope is exactly the two wait sites (the 1.1 helper `_await_inbox` and `_await_approval`); the round loop's inline drain calls (5529/5629) are one-shot reads, not waits, and stay as-is. The plan's gate is a latency test with a simulated writer plus a no-busy-loop CPU check; the engine is stdlib-only — no watchdog/kqueue dependencies, a stat poll is the sanctioned mechanism.
subtasks: orchestrator.py: change `_await_inbox` and `_await_approval` default poll to 0.25s; inside the loop, replace per-tick content reads with an os.stat (st_mtime_ns, st_size) comparison against the last-seen tuple for human_inbox.txt; only on change (or first tick) read the file to test non-emptiness.
Keep decision-file checks as os.path.exists per tick (measure: 3 exists + 1 stat per 250ms is negligible; document the measurement in the PR).
Handle the missing-file case: stat OSError == 'unchanged', never crashes the wait loop.
Make the tick injectable (parameter with default 0.25) so tests can compress time.
tests/test_conversational.py (extend): latency test — writer thread writes human_inbox.txt after 300ms; assert the waiter returns in < 0.75s wall-clock.

CPU regression test: run the wait loop idle for ~2s with a counter-instrumented read function; assert zero content reads occurred while the file was unchanged; additionally assert time.process_time() delta over the idle window stays under a small bound (e.g. < 50ms).
Run `make verify`.
acceptance_criteria: A message written to human_inbox.txt during a conversational wait wakes the engine in < 0.75s (test-proven at the default tick).

Approval waits (_await_approval) also tick at ~250ms; the approval decision-file contract (.ok/.edit/.changes semantics, stale-file clearing at 6363–6367, state management) is byte-identical in behavior.
While the inbox is unchanged, the wait loop performs zero full-file content reads (counter-proven), and idle CPU over the wait is bounded by the test.
A deleted or never-created human_inbox.txt never crashes the wait loop.
Timeout semantics (return value, state cleanup, emitted messages) are unchanged from 1.1/_await_approval.
Full existing suite green — non-conversational workflows see no behavioral change beyond faster approval wake.
QA verifies: run the 1.1 scripted-inbox test unchanged — it still passes with the new cadence.
test_plan: Gate (from plan): latency test with simulated writer; no busy-loop CPU regression.
tests/test_conversational.py: wake-latency assertion (< 0.75s), zero-idle-reads counter assertion, process_time bound assertion, missing-file robustness case.
`make verify` green.

tasks.title: GUI: per-chat history — re-key OrchestratorStore chat persistence
tasks.goal: Chat history persistence moves from one global Application Support file to per-chat keys so two chats can never bleed into each other, with the existing concierge history preserved as the Home chat's history.
tasks.context: Verified anchors: `chatMessages` @Published with `didSet { saveChatHistory() }` at OrchestratorStore.swift:628–629; `chatHistoryURL` = Application Support/Orchestrator/chat_history.json (:2946–2949); saveChatHistory (:2951), loadChatHistory (:2962, called from init at :778), startNewChat (:2972). ChatHome.send() (ChatHome.swift:195–230) appends to store.chatMessages from an async Task — an in-flight concierge reply can land AFTER the user switches chats, so the reply must be delivered to the chat it belongs to, not whatever is current (rulebook §12.2). Design: introduce a current-chat key (e.g. `currentChatKey: String`, default 'home' for the legacy concierge conversation) and store files at Application Support/Orchestrator/chat_history/<key>.json; migrate the legacy chat_history.json to chat_history/home.json once, on first load, without deleting the original until the new file is written. Trap verified in code: loadChatHistory assigns chatMessages, which fires didSet → saveChatHistory — with per-chat keys a load-during-switch could write chat A's messages under chat B's key; guard with an isLoadingHistory flag or write-through only when the key matches the loaded key.
subtasks: OrchestratorStore.swift: add `currentChatKey` (default 'home'); change chatHistoryURL into `chatHistoryURL(for key:)` → Application Support/Orchestrator/chat_history/<key>.json; keep the directory-creation behavior of saveChatHistory.

Re-key saveChatHistory/loadChatHistory to the current key; add a switchChat(to:) that saves the outgoing chat, updates the key, then loads the incoming chat — with a load-guard so didSet-triggered saves during load cannot cross-write keys.
One-shot migration in loadChatHistory: if chat_history/<home>.json is absent and legacy chat_history.json exists, copy it to home.json (leave the legacy file in place, harmless).

Tag in-flight concierge replies with the chat key they were sent from (capture the key alongside the existing `let store = self.store` in ChatHome.send(), ChatHome.swift:210) and deliver to that key's history — appending to the visible chatMessages only when the key is still current.

tasks.title: GUI: chat-session lifecycle — mint flat chat dir, launch/supervise engine run, honest states
tasks.goal: The store can mint a flat chat dir (0.2 naming), launch a conversational engine run for it, and surface its full lifecycle (launching/running/waiting/stopped/crashed/relaunching) as an explicit state model — a crash is a visible error, never silence.
tasks.context: Verified precedents to reuse, not reinvent: `createFactoryApp` (OrchestratorStore.swift:3350–3391) mints `<slug>/initial_prompt/initial_prompt.md` + `workflow.txt`; `runProject` (:3049) → `launch(args:project:)` (:3123–3178) spawns `python3 orchestrator.py --root <root> --app <name>` with API-key env stripping (:3134–3140), pipes output to runLog, and a terminationHandler (:3158) that reports the exit code — that handler is where crash detection hooks in; `stopProject` (:3075, SIGTERM→5s→SIGKILL + owner-checked lock cleanup) and `stopRun` (:3307, lock-pid path). Chat dir naming per 0.2: slugified components joined with literal `--`, uniqueness via suffixing (ChatHome.swift:236–240 precedent). The minted dir must satisfy find_apps (initial_prompt/initial_prompt.md, orchestrator.py:6420) and set workflow.txt to chat_ideas/chat_research; the first user message is the initial prompt body. Relaunch of an existing chat uses the engine's resume path (prepare_resume, orchestrator.py:7801; conversational resume is append-only per 1.1). Rulebook R4/§4.2: model the lifecycle as one enum on a per-chat model, not scattered booleans; R2: 'running' may only be shown while a live pid/lock or Process handle proves it.
subtasks: Add a ChatSession model (id = chat dir name, project/section/slug components, state enum: idle, launching, running, waitingForHuman, stopping, stopped, crashed(exitCode: Int32), relaunching) — one enum, no loose booleans.

OrchestratorStore: `mintChatSession(project:section:title:workflow:firstMessage:)` — build the flat name per 0.2 (component-wise slugify + literal '--', uniqueness suffixing), write initial_prompt/initial_prompt.md (first message as body) + workflow.txt, refuse and surface an error if the dir exists.

tasks.title: Fork verb — copy a session dir minus locks and minus agent-thread ids
tasks.goal: A fork copies a chat/session dir to a new uniquely-named flat dir with all transcripts and state intact, but with zero lock files and zero agent-thread continuity carriers — so a forked session can never resume another session's CLI agent thread.
tasks.context: Safety rationale, verified in code: `codex exec resume` always runs workspace-write regardless of the original session's sandbox (call_agent_sessioned docstring, orchestrator.py:1543–1547) — resuming a cloned thread id in a read-only phase would silently upgrade its sandbox. Where thread ids actually live, verified: the in-memory maps cfg['_claude_sessions']/'_codex_sessions' (seeded at :5374–5375, used at :1561–1575) do NOT persist to agent_state.json (checked load_state:2622–2647 — no session fields); the on-disk continuity carrier is `<app>/.agent_cwd/` (cfg['_session_cwd'] = app_dir/.agent_cwd at :5381) — the stable cwd that claude CLI keys its session store by. So the copy must exclude: `.agent_cwd/` entirely, every `*.lock` file anywhere in the tree, and pending `approvals/*` decision files (they'd instantly answer the fork's first checkpoint); and must sanitize agent_state.json: runner_pid=None, awaiting_approval=None, error=None (fields verified in load_state). Reset human_inbox.txt to empty — an undrained message would double-deliver (once in source, once in fork). Root locks (<root>/.orch-locks/<name>.lock) are keyed by dir name, so a new unique name (0.2 suffixing rule) avoids collision by construction. Place the helper engine-side so CLI and GUI share it; GUI action calls it then refreshes.
subtasks: orchestrator.py (or a small sessions helper module): fork_session(root, src_slug, new_slug=None) — derive new_slug (src + '-fork', then 0.2 uniqueness suffixing); copytree with an ignore function excluding '.agent_cwd', any name ending in '.lock', and 'approvals'; then truncate human_inbox.txt and rewrite agent_state.json with runner_pid/awaiting_approval/error cleared.

Refuse to fork a dir that is currently locked-running IF the copy could tear mid-write: read the source's lock; if live, either refuse with a message or document why a torn fork is acceptable — pick refuse (honest, simple) and surface it.

Engine side: search.py (new, stdlib sqlite3 only) keeps an FTS5 table of message rows; incremental indexing tracks a per-session byte offset into messages.jsonl so re-index cost is O(new lines); message CONTENT for indexing is read via each line's content_path (the JSONL is an index, not a body store — 2.4 contract). tasks.title: (radar adopt) LLM trace schema: every runner call writes traces/<run>/<seq>.json, crash-valid from the first byte
tasks.goal: Every runner invocation writes a redacted JSON trace file <app_dir>/traces/<run_id>/<seq>.json {schema_version, trace_id, parent_call, ts, app, phase, round, agent, producer, model, rendered_prompt, response, stderr, exit, tokens, duration_s, status} — written as a valid 'started' record BEFORE the runner runs and atomically finalized after, so a kill mid-call always leaves parseable evidence. The schema ships NOW (drill-down UI is V3.1): retrofitting call-level logging after autonomy ships would make the first overnight failures undebuggable.
tasks.context: Radar ADOPT NOW #5 (LangSmith/AgentOps observability). Verified single chokepoint: every orchestrated turn funnels through _call_agent_once (orchestrator.py:1337), whose one runner dispatch is :1430 (`out, err, code, command = resolve_runner(agent)(cfg, prompt, timeout)`); fallback retries re-enter _call_agent_once from call_agent's ladder (:1257, :1269). Key drift/gap vs a naive reading: the rendered prompt is persisted NOWHERE today — write_call_log (:1024–1048) stores redacted command/stdout/stderr in the ENGINE-GLOBAL logs/ dir (pruned after 14 days, prune_logs :1051), and the command string shows '<prompt on stdin>' (:672/:733/:959) with parts truncated at 120 chars (_display_cmd :1013). Traces are per-app, additive, and must pass schemas.redact_secrets before disk — mirror the §17 single-chokepoint precedent at :1470–1471. Tokens: CLI runners report none; run_local (:962–995) currently DISCARDS Ollama's prompt_eval_count/eval_count (:988 reads only 'response'). Do NOT change the runner 4-tuple: it is unpacked at :1430, :2977, :8136 and stubbed as a 4-tuple in tests/test_events.py:141 — use a thread-local side-channel instead. parent_call travels as an explicit function argument, never a new cfg["_ key (2.3 grep gate). Auxiliary direct runner calls (:2977 advisory probe, :8136 concierge) bypass call_agent and are explicitly untraced.
subtasks: New traces.py (stdlib-only): a locked module-level TraceWriter; run_id minted once per (process, app_dir) as '<UTC %Y%m%d_%H%M%S>-<pid>' (crash-resume gets a new run dir — that is the debugging boundary wanted); zero-padded per-run seq; write_started(...) creates <seq>.json via tmp-file + os.replace with status='started' and the redacted rendered_prompt; finalize(...) atomically rewrites with response/stderr/exit/tokens/duration_s/status ('ok'|'error'). Valid JSON exists on disk at every instant. Module docstring documents that GC is task 8.6's policy (traces accumulate until then, deliberately).

orchestrator.py _call_agent_once (:1337): call traces.write_started immediately before the dispatch at :1430 with {app, phase, round, agent, producer=str(agent), model=_primary_model_label(cfg, agent) (:1148), rendered_prompt=prompt, parent_call}; finalize exactly once per started record by threading it through the existing exception arms (:1431–1466), the empty-output/banner failure paths (:1474–1494), the success path (:1495–1500), and the finally at :1501 — mirroring the one-turn_completed-per-turn_started invariant documented at :1411–1416.

parent_call threading without cfg keys: _call_agent_once gains keyword arg parent_call=None; when _call_agent_once raises AgentError it attaches the failed call's trace id to the exception (exc.trace_id = …; AgentError is a plain Exception subclass at :164 — attribute assignment is safe); call_agent's fallback loop (:1229–1277) reads exc.trace_id and passes it as parent_call into each retry's _call_agent_once, chaining rescue attempts to the primary.

Tokens side-channel: traces.set_last_usage(dict)/pop_last_usage() on threading.local; run_local (:962–995) populates {prompt_tokens: prompt_eval_count, completion_tokens: eval_count} from the Ollama response body before returning; _call_agent_once pops it after dispatch into the trace's tokens field; all CLI runners leave tokens null — never fabricated (6.4 owns richer usage capture later).

Redaction + never-crash: rendered_prompt, response, and stderr pass schemas.redact_secrets before any write (chokepoint parity with :1470–1471); every traces.py entry point is wrapped so a trace failure emits one WARN (write_call_log's :1047–1048 precedent) and never takes a turn down.

Tests (tests/test_traces.py): stub runner via the RUNNERS-patch pattern (tests/test_events.py:134–141) — one started+finalized trace per call with every schema field; fallback chain — primary raises, rescue succeeds, child trace's parent_call == primary trace_id and primary's status='error'; kill-mid-call — runner stub raises SystemExit/KeyboardInterrupt-adjacent hard failure before finalize, assert <seq>.json parses as valid JSON with status='started'; planted fake secret in prompt+response never reaches any trace byte; seq strictly monotonic and file-unique under a ThreadPoolExecutor parallel round.
Run the golden transcript suite (tests/test_transcript_golden.py) + full suite + make verify: traces must not alter one transcript or event byte.

tasks.title: Lineage + versioning + bus-level loop guards (depth caps, convergence, branch+reconcile)
tasks.goal: Give the store real version semantics: supersedes chains with content hashes, lineage depth + hop counts enforced at publish time, identical descendants auto-marked converged, concurrent derivations forced into named branches with a mandatory reconcile artifact, and a latest-final resolver that refuses to guess on unreconciled branches.
tasks.context: Loop control lives ON THE BUS (sections plan §4: content-hash dedup, lineage depth caps default 4, per-chain hop budgets) so no consumer — manual today, Conductor in M7 — can bypass it; 7.2's pre-route guards READ the meta fields this task writes (sequencing constraint #4 in the engineering plan). All work is in artifacts.py on top of 4.1's meta fields. Versioning model: re-publishing a derivation sets version=v(n+1), supersedes=v(n)'s id, lineage=ancestor id chain; content_hash is a sha256 of body.md. Publish-time enforcement: depth > cap → publish REFUSED with a loud error; content_hash identical to the direct ancestor → artifact status auto-set 'converged' and it must never be eligible for routing (4.5) or trigger re-derivation. Concurrency: per-lineage advisory flock (guard file artifacts/.lineage-<root-id>.lock, fcntl pattern orchestrator.py:377–422); if two writers derive from the same version anyway, the second publish becomes a named branch (v3-a/v3-b) — never a silent overwrite — and the store requires a 'reconcile'-type artifact (registry type from 4.1) before the lineage has a 'latest final' again. latest_final(project_dir, lineage_root) REFUSES (explicit LineageBranchedError or error return listing the branch ids) while branches are unreconciled — it must never silently pick a winner. Consumers seeing a superseded version get a staleness signal: is_stale(meta) helper here; the GUI badge is 4.9.
subtasks: In artifacts.py implement derive/publish-version path: publish(..., supersedes=<id>) computes version, lineage[], depth, hop_count, content_hash (sha256 of body bytes) and writes them into meta.json.
Enforce the depth cap at publish time (default 4, overridable via the type registry): over-cap publish returns a refusal error; nothing is written.

Implement content-hash convergence: if the new body hash equals the direct ancestor's, publish succeeds but status='converged'; add is_routable(meta) that returns False for converged artifacts so 4.5/7.2 share one predicate.

Implement per-lineage advisory flock: derivations from the same lineage serialize on artifacts/.lineage-<root>.lock; a writer that finds its parent version already superseded when it acquires the lock publishes as a named branch (suffix -a/-b in version) instead of a second linear v(n+1).

Require reconciliation: while a lineage has >1 unreconciled branch head, latest_final() raises/returns an explicit branched-lineage error naming both heads; publishing a 'reconcile'-type artifact whose meta lists both branch heads as parents merges the lineage and restores latest_final.
Implement is_stale(project_dir, meta): True when meta's artifact is superseded by a newer non-branch version (consumed-version staleness for 4.9's badge and 4.7's retrieval preference).

Tests: two-writer collision fixture (fork/threads) proving branch+reconcile with no silent pick; depth-cap fixture; identical-descendant → converged fixture; latest_final refusal fixture; reconcile-restores-resolution fixture.
acceptance_criteria: Publishing a derivation writes version, supersedes, lineage[], depth, hop_count, content_hash into meta.json; all values verifiable from fixtures.
A publish that would exceed the lineage depth cap (default 4) is refused with an explicit error and writes nothing — it must NOT silently truncate or reset the chain.
A descendant whose content hash equals its direct ancestor's is auto-marked status='converged'; is_routable() returns False for it; it can never trigger another derivation hop.
Two writers deriving concurrently from the same version yield two NAMED branches (e.g. v3-a, v3-b) — never a lost update, never a silent second v3.
latest_final() on a branched, unreconciled lineage REFUSES with an error naming the branch heads; it never silently picks one branch.
Publishing a reconcile artifact referencing both heads restores latest_final() to the reconcile artifact.
All lineage state lives in meta.json files — no new database, no in-memory-only state (crash-safe by construction; killing a writer mid-derivation leaves the store readable and the lock releasable).

tasks.title: Return edge + @-mention delegation: Quick-take vs Deep-dive tiers in the composer
tasks.goal: Typing @Research <question> in any chat composer fires delegation: Quick-take (guest persona answers in one turn, seconds) or Deep-dive (4.4-minted sub-session running the target section's real workflow; the reply artifact card lands back in the originating chat, async).
tasks.context: The design line (sections plan §7): a persona is an OPINION, a section is a PROCESS — the two tiers must be visibly distinct because a guest persona will confidently improvise research it never did. Deep-dive = exactly 4.4's mint_delegation_session with reply_to=originating session dir + route of the question as context (4.5's push format); the reply card arrives via 4.4's human_inbox return edge and renders in the transcript when the inbox drains. Quick-take = a single guest-persona turn using 3.5's cross-section cast resolution ('research:investigator' syntax) inside the CURRENT session — no sub-session, no artifact. Composer surface: built by 1.7 (composer under a live debate, TranscriptView.swift) and 1.5/1.6 (chat lifecycle/rendering) — VERIFY its final shape in the repo when you start; today's TranscriptView.swift (419 lines) has MessageBubble at :214 and PendingHumanBubble at :259 but no composer yet, and ChatHome.swift still holds the one-shot conciergeAsk (:212) that 1.6 replaces. Engine side: @-mention parsing belongs in the engine's inbox-drain path (drain_human_inbox, orchestrator.py:2592) or a thin pre-drain hook — NOT in Swift — so CLI users get the same verb. GUI offers the tier choice explicitly at send time. A pending Deep-dive must render as an honest in-flight state and resolve to the card or to a visible failure (4.4's failed status).
subtasks: Engine: parse '@<SectionName> <question>' at the inbox-drain boundary (hook beside drain_human_inbox, orchestrator.py:2592); unknown section name → the message is treated as plain chat text plus a visible warning line in the transcript (never silently dropped, never a crash).

Engine Deep-dive path: on parse, call 4.4's mint_delegation_session(reply_to=this session) + push the question as the minted session's seed context (4.5 format) + spawn; the originating debate continues (async by design).

Engine Quick-take path: resolve the target section's designated guest persona via 3.5's cross-section role resolution and run ONE extra roster turn in the current phase, persona-chipped; no artifact, no sub-session.

GUI composer: '@' triggers a section-name autocomplete; on send, an explicit tier picker (Quick take — one turn, opinion only / Deep dive — real sub-session, returns a brief) with the plan's honest copy; the choice is encoded in the inbox message so the engine needs no side channel.

GUI pending state: a Deep-dive in flight renders as a pending card (spinner + target section + started-at); it resolves to the artifact card when the reply lands, or to a visible failed card when delegation.json reports failure — it must never spin forever.

Copy the shape, not the code: artifacts.retrieve(project_dir, query_text, max_chars, top_k, sensitivity_filter) scoring meta keywords[] (×3) + body terms, restricted to status=='final' (4.8's predicate) and non-stale versions (prefer latest via 4.3's resolver; a branched lineage contributes NOTHING rather than guessing — 4.3's refusal propagates as an on_error note). tasks.title: Admission control: per-type finalization policy; only final artifacts route or retrieve
tasks.goal: The type registry gains a per-type finalization policy {auto_final_on_consensus, requires_review_gate, requires_human}; publish assigns status from the policy, explicit transitions move draft→final, and one shared predicate makes 4.5/4.7 (and later 7.2) admit only final artifacts.
tasks.context: Sections plan gap #9: bus admission control — half-formed ideas must not auto-flow between sections. All logic lives in artifacts.py against 4.1's registry (artifact_types.json) so every consumer shares one enforcement point; 4.5 and 4.7 were built to call a final-only predicate — this task is where that predicate becomes policy-driven. Semantics: auto_final_on_consensus → an artifact published from a phase that ended CONSENSUS: YES (the publish hook in 4.2 knows the phase's consensus flag from run_debate_phase's return — thread it into meta.source or a publish kwarg) gets status 'final' immediately; requires_review_gate → published as 'pending_review', finalized by an explicit finalize() call (the review gate itself — e.g. a QA-section pass — is a later consumer; the mechanism here is the status transition API); requires_human → published as 'pending_review', finalized ONLY by an explicit human action (GUI button lands in 4.9; CLI finalize with --by-human flag here). Transitions are recorded in meta.json (status_history: [{status, at, by}]) so provenance shows WHO finalized. Illegal transitions (final→draft, finalizing an already-final artifact) are refused loudly. 4.3's 'converged' status is orthogonal and must not be overwritten by finalization.
subtasks: Extend artifact_types.json seeds: each type carries finalization: one of {auto_final_on_consensus, requires_review_gate, requires_human}; registry loader validates the enum and reports unknown values via on_error (falling back to the SAFEST policy, requires_human, with a report — never silently to auto).
In publish (4.2 hook): thread the phase's consensus outcome into the publish call; assign initial status per policy (final vs pending_review).

Implement finalize(project_dir, artifact_id, by) with legal-transition checking and status_history append; implement is_admissible(meta) = status=='final' and is_routable(meta) (4.3) — the ONE predicate 4.5/4.7/7.2 use.
Swap 4.5's and 4.7's direct status checks to is_admissible.
Thin CLI hook for human finalization (argparse: finalize <project> <artifact-id>) so the flow works before 4.9's GUI button.

Tests: policy matrix (3 policies × consensus yes/no → expected initial status); illegal-transition refusals; pending_review artifacts invisible to route_push and retrieve; finalize flips visibility; status_history recorded.

Subprocess mechanics: procutil.run_capture (procutil.py:123) runs a command in a fresh process group with timeout-kills-the-tree semantics and returns (out, err, returncode) — use it, never bare subprocess. The llm_rules + bounded-retry shape already exists in the engine: run_phase_quality_gate (orchestrator.py:2155) is one call_agent turn graded by anchored regexes (QUALITY_PASS_RE/QUALITY_FAIL_RE, orchestrator.py:3393–3394) inside a bounded repair loop (orchestrator.py:5690–5751) that records honest quality_gate_fail metadata on exhaustion — copy that shape at publish scope. The producing-turn retry hooks in at the post-phase site where 4.2 publishes (_record_phase_contracts region, orchestrator.py:6135). Two closed registries need explicit extension: events.KINDS (events.py:49; unknown kinds warn and are invisible to filtered reads) and mistakes.CLASSES (mistakes.py:52). subtasks: Gate config: load <workspace>/hooks.json plus sections/<name>/hooks.json (3.1 manifest dir) — each {hooks: [{matcher: {artifact_types[], sections[]}, command, timeout_s}], llm_rules: [{id, rule, applies_to[]}]}; absent files mean an empty gate; a CORRUPT config file fails CLOSED: publishes quarantine with reason 'gate config unreadable' plus a visible banner event — never a silent fail-open.

Deterministic hooks runner in artifacts.py: for each matching hook run the command via procutil.run_capture (procutil.py:123) with stdin = one JSON object {body, meta} and a timeout (default 30s); exit 0 = allow; exit 2 = block, with stderr captured as feedback (schemas.redact_secrets, schemas.py:300, then length-capped); any OTHER exit code, timeout, or spawn failure = hook_error — surfaced as a visible banner event + mistakes line, does NOT block (document this Claude Code-style contract in the config file header so operators write hooks accordingly).

Semantic guardrail: evaluate matching llm_rules in ONE cheap agent turn (config knob to route it to a local model via the existing runner resolution; run_local at orchestrator.py:962 returns the standard (out, err, code, cmd) shape) rendering the rules + artifact body into a verdict prompt; parse 'GATE: PASS'/'GATE: FAIL' with anchored regexes exactly like QUALITY_PASS_RE (orchestrator.py:3393); an unparseable verdict counts as FAIL with reason 'unparseable verdict' (fail-closed, loud).

Bounded retry-with-feedback: on any block (hook exit 2 or llm-rule FAIL), re-run the producing agent turn once (runtime.gate_retry_limit, default 1) with an '===== GATE FEEDBACK (fix and re-emit the artifact) =====' block containing the hook stderr / rule failures appended to the producing prompt; re-extract and re-gate the new artifact block. Feedback threads via arguments/TurnContext — grep gate: zero new cfg["_ writes.

Quarantine: after retries are exhausted, publish the artifact WITH status='quarantined' and meta.gate = {attempts, failures: [{source: hook|llm_rule, id, feedback}]}; 4.8's is_admissible must return False for quarantined artifacts (they never route via 4.5 or retrieve via 4.7); the artifact stays on disk, fully inspectable — a blocked artifact is evidence, not garbage.

tasks.title: Artifact→slot ingestion (SUBSCRIBE mode): docs render pulls final artifacts via doc_map slot mappings
tasks.goal: docs.py render passively ingests published `final` artifacts from artifacts.py according to doc_map slot mappings, so a doc can render from artifacts ALONE — the mechanism the gap-report work queue (5.4, 7.5) depends on.
tasks.context: DRIFT NOTE (verified): artifacts.py does NOT exist yet and events.py KINDS (events.py:49–58) has no artifact_* kinds — 4.1 (artifact store: workspace/<project>/artifacts/<id>/ body.md + meta.json), 4.3 (lineage/content_hash/'latest final' resolver that REFUSES on unreconciled branches), and 4.8 (only `final` artifacts route/retrieve) are hard prerequisites; verify their actual APIs before coding and trust them over this card. tasks.title: Doc-slot ownership manifest: one owning section per blueprint slot; conflicts become gap artifacts
tasks.goal: Every blueprint slot has exactly one owning section declared in the doc map; when final artifacts from different lineages contend for one slot, the render emits a structured `gap` artifact describing the conflict — never last-write-wins, never a silent pick.
tasks.context: This implements sections-plan gap #10 (orchestrator-v3-sections-plan.md:372–374): 'one section owns each blueprint slot; cross-lineage conflicts surface as gap artifacts (never silent last-write-wins) and are listed loudly in the quiescence report.' It builds directly on 5.2's ingestion: 5.2 already handles same-lineage versioning via 4.3's latest-final resolver (refusal on unreconciled branches); 5.3 adds the cross-lineage case — two `final` artifacts with disjoint lineage[] chains both matching one slot. Ownership lives in doc_map.json's slots[] owner_section field (reserved in 5.1's schema); populate it for all 40 slots from the section taxonomy (sections-plan §2: e.g. product slots→ideas/planning, architecture→build/design, QA→qa, GTM→go-to-market, legal→legal). Distinguish two failure modes with different renders: unowned slot (owner_section missing/unknown — a doc-map lint error, banner + skip-from-conflict-resolution) vs contended slot (multiple lineages → conflict). The conflict `gap` artifact is published through artifacts.py's normal publish path (4.1) with type 'gap', and must be idempotent across re-renders: derive a deterministic dedupe key (slot_id + sorted contending content_hashes) and skip publishing if an open gap artifact with that key already exists — otherwise every render spams a new gap. Rendered slot shows an explicit conflict note naming both artifact ids. Routing the gap anywhere is 5.4/M7's job, not this card's.

tasks.title: Gap report generation: empty/thin slots become structured gap artifacts routed (manually) to owning sections
tasks.goal: Every render produces an honest gap report: each empty or thin blueprint slot yields a structured `gap` artifact addressed to its owning section, plus a human-readable GAP_REPORT.md — the work queue the Conductor's goal predicate (7.5) will consume.
tasks.context: The sections plan makes this the engine of the global loop: 'The Documentation gap report IS the work queue: each empty doc slot generates a fill request routed to the owning section' (orchestrator-v3-sections-plan.md:153–155), and M7's termination layer 1 is 'gap report empty + DoD checklists + evalharness threshold' — so the gap artifact schema here is a stability contract for 7.5; keep it additive-only once landed. Builds on 5.2 (slot fill states) and 5.3 (owner_section per slot, conflict gaps with dedupe keys). Definitions must be explicit, not vibes: EMPTY = no final artifact matched and no phase output fed the slot; THIN = filled but body under the slot's min_chars (the field reserved in 5.1's schema; default e.g. 200, per-slot overridable in doc_map.json — data, not code). Reuse 5.3's publish path and idempotency mechanism: dedupe_key = hash(slot_id + reason + content_hash-of-current-fill-or-empty) so a re-render with unchanged state publishes nothing, while a slot that gains content and later thins again produces a fresh gap. 'Routed manually for now' means: the gap artifact's meta names the owning section (route target data), but nothing auto-injects it anywhere — a human uses M4's Send-to/drag verbs; do NOT wire Conductor or inbox writes. GAP_REPORT.md is a deterministic docs.py render in the KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md style (docs.py:494): honest, non-AI, nothing inferred.

tasks.goal: A Notion export is an explicit, two-step operation in docsync.py: step 1 always produces a dry-run diff of what would change versus the last exported snapshot; step 2 (delivery) runs only with separate explicit authorization — never fire-and-forget.

epic.title: Conductor (global autonomous mode)
epic.goal: Build conductor.py — a separate small stdlib process, one per workspace — that routes final artifacts between sections via data-driven rules, mints sessions through 4.4's helper, enforces per-section capability manifests, terminates via a four-layer stack (goal predicate / quiescence / budgets / stall), and is governed by oversight dials with loops-gated as default. Sections stay strictly sequential internally; the Conductor provides concurrency ACROSS sections. It polls authoritative agent_state.json and treats events.jsonl only as a wake-up hint.
epic.exit_gate: Seed one idea at 11pm in loops-gated mode; by morning it is researched, planned, and documented (5.0's Documentation section closes the loop); Mission Control replays the night; every external side-effect sat in the pending queue; `git reset` cleanly unwinds it.

tasks.title: Stop coverage for runs the GUI didn't launch (nested + Conductor-minted), plus engine run.pid
tasks.goal: Any run — GUI-launched, CLI-launched, shepherd-launched, Conductor-minted, flat or nested — can be stopped from the GUI after a GUI relaunch, and the engine leaves a per-session run.pid file as a belt-and-braces kill target when the lock is unreadable.
tasks.context: Verified against current code (anchors match the plan, no drift): the GUI's stopRun (gui/Sources/OrchestratorGUI/OrchestratorStore.swift:3307–3342) already handles foreign runs — if canStop(name) it takes the GUI-owned stopProject path, otherwise it reads the pid from appLocks (populated by FactoryScanner.scanLocks, OrchestratorStore.swift:401–430, which parses `pid=`/`started=` from `.orch-locks/<name>.lock` payloads), confirms liveness with kill(pid,0) so it never SIGTERMs a recycled pid, then SIGTERM → 5s → SIGKILL → clearLockFile. Engine side: locks are per-app `<root>/.orch-locks/<app>.lock` (acquire_app_lock orchestrator.py:375, _app_lock_path :358, LOCKS_DIR re-pointed to the workspace at :8037–8038); the SIGTERM handler _cleanup (:8160–8170) sets _SHUTDOWN, calls procutil.kill_live_groups(), and removes held locks; save_state writes state["runner_pid"]=os.getpid() on every save (:2720). There is NO run.pid file anywhere today (grep-verified). The gap: lock names are the FLAT app dir name, so 3.0's nested `workspace/<project>/<section>/<chat-slug>/` dirs need collision-free lock names the scanner and stopRun can map back to a session dir, and Conductor-minted runs (7.2 via 4.4's helper) must be stoppable the same way. Trap: the lock payload's pid can go stale after crash — that is exactly why run.pid in the session dir is belt-and-braces, and why the existing liveness check must be preserved, not weakened.

tasks.title: conductor.py skeleton: single-instance loop, wake-on-events, resumable state + routing ledger
tasks.goal: A new stdlib-only conductor.py runs as exactly one process per workspace, wakes on events.jsonl growth, polls authoritative agent_state.json, persists conductor_state.json plus an append-only routing ledger JSONL, and resumes correctly after being killed at any loop stage.
tasks.context: Greenfield file (verified: no conductor.py exists). Product contract is orchestrator-v3-sections-plan.md §5: 'polls authoritative state (agent_state.json) and treats events.jsonl only as a wake-up hint' — events lines are capped/truncatable (events.py _MAX_EVENT_LINE_BYTES=3500, :63) and carry ids+paths only, so decisions must NEVER be made from event payloads alone. Mechanisms to reuse, verified in code: single-instance via fcntl.flock on a workspace-level guard file — precedent is acquire_app_lock's flock'd guard (orchestrator.py:375–430); events live at `<app_dir>/events.jsonl` (events.py EVENTS_FILENAME :46, emit_event :89); per-session state read via the agent_state.json shape in load_state (orchestrator.py:2622–2661 — fields current_phase, done, error, awaiting_approval, runner_pid); atomic state writes via the save_state per-writer-tmp + os.replace pattern (:2718–2726). The skeleton owns: the wake loop (sum of events.jsonl sizes across sessions as a cheap growth signal + a bounded poll interval), conductor_state.json (ledger cursor, per-session last-seen state hash, explicit lifecycle enum), and the ledger JSONL that 7.3 will make idempotency-bearing. Trap: the ledger append and conductor_state cursor update are two writes — crash between them is the case 7.3 formalizes; the skeleton must already order writes so replay is safe (append ledger first, cursor second, dedupe on resume).
subtasks: Create conductor.py with argparse (--root, --once, --interval), stdlib-only imports, and a module docstring stating the authoritative-state-vs-events-hint contract.
Implement single-instance guard: fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB) on `<root>/.orchestrator/conductor.lock` held for process lifetime; a second copy exits with a clear message, exit code nonzero.
Implement workspace scan: enumerate session dirs (nested layout from 3.0 + legacy flat), read each agent_state.json defensively (missing/corrupt file = skip with visible warning, never crash).
Implement wake mechanism: cheap mtime/size sweep of events.jsonl files at a short tick; a growth triggers an immediate full authoritative-state poll; otherwise poll at --interval.

Implement conductor_state.json with an explicit loop-stage enum (scanning / evaluating / acting / idle), ledger cursor, and per-session digests; write atomically via tmp + os.replace (save_state pattern, orchestrator.py:2718).

Implement routing ledger: append-only `<root>/.orchestrator/conductor_ledger.jsonl`, one JSON object per line {ts, stage, decision, session, detail} — ordering rule: ledger append BEFORE conductor_state cursor advance.

tasks.title: Route idempotency: deterministic route_id, ledger-before-act, restart dedup
tasks.goal: Every route gets a deterministic route_id = hash(artifact, target, rule); the id is written to the ledger BEFORE any side effect, inbox injections carry the route_id marker, and a restarted conductor never re-executes a route that already fired.
tasks.context: This formalizes the crash-safety ordering 7.1 sketched. The side effects a route performs are (a) minting+launching a session via 4.4's helper and (b) injecting an artifact reference into a session's human_inbox.txt — the engine folds that inbox into the live conversation via drain_human_inbox (orchestrator.py:2592–2613, verified): it reads the whole file, truncates it, and appends the text as a '**You (human) — …**' block. Once drained, the injected text is gone from the inbox — so restart dedup CANNOT rely on re-reading the inbox; the ledger is the source of truth, and the route_id marker embedded in the injected payload exists so a human or tool reading the transcript can trace the injection back to a ledger line. Protocol: (1) compute route_id from stable inputs (artifact id+content_hash, target section/session, rule id) — same inputs always same id; (2) append 'intent' ledger line with route_id; (3) perform the side effect, embedding the route_id marker in the injected inbox text and in the minted session's metadata; (4) append 'done' ledger line. On restart: intent-without-done means the effect MAY have happened — recovery must probe (does the minted dir exist? does the marker appear in the target's transcript/inbox?) before re-acting, and must ledger whichever way it resolves. The plan's gate is exactly the crash-between-append-and-record test.
subtasks: Implement route_id: sha256 over a canonical JSON of {artifact_id, artifact_content_hash, target, rule_id}, truncated to a readable prefix; unit-test determinism and sensitivity (any input change → different id).
Restructure route execution in conductor.py into the intent→act→done ledger protocol; the intent line carries the full route context so replay needs no other state.

Embed `[route:<route_id>]` markers in every inbox injection payload and in minted-session metadata (via 4.4 helper's meta), so effects are traceable post-drain (drain_human_inbox truncates the inbox — orchestrator.py:2605–2607).

Implement restart recovery: for each intent-without-done ledger entry, probe for the effect (minted dir exists / marker present in target session dir), then ledger 'recovered-done' or re-execute and ledger normally; never blind re-execute.
Dedup guard: before acting on any route, check the ledger for an existing done/recovered-done with the same route_id; skip with a ledgered dedup line.

Write the crash-between-append-and-record test: kill the conductor after the intent append but before the effect, after the effect but before done, and after done; restart each time; assert exactly-once effect in all three cases.

Add a re-publish test: the same artifact re-evaluated on a later pass (unchanged content_hash) produces the same route_id and is deduped; a genuinely new version (new content_hash) produces a new route_id and routes.
files: orchestrator.py:2592-2613 (drain_human_inbox — the drain path the marker must survive tracing through)

acceptance_criteria: route_id is deterministic: identical (artifact, content_hash, target, rule) always yields the identical id across process restarts; any component change yields a different id.

Kill after intent-before-effect: restart probes, finds no effect, executes exactly once. Kill after effect-before-done: restart probes, finds the marker/dir, records recovered-done, does NOT execute again. Kill after done: restart is a no-op for that route. All three verified by the crash test.
Re-evaluating an already-routed artifact (same content_hash) is a ledgered dedup skip — the target session must NOT receive a second inbox injection or a second minted dir.
A new version of the artifact (different content_hash) is a NEW route, not a dedup.

Inbox injections carry the route_id marker; because drain_human_inbox truncates the inbox after folding (orchestrator.py:2605), recovery probing checks the target session dir/transcript, never assumes the inbox still holds the text.
Recovery never silently drops an ambiguous route: if the probe cannot determine whether the effect happened, it surfaces the ambiguity (ledger + visible banner) rather than guessing.
QA verifies via the crash-between-append-and-record kill matrix.

tasks.title: Capability/permission model: per-section {writes, exec, external}, engine-enforced, pending-actions queue
tasks.goal: Each section manifest declares its capabilities {writes, exec, external}; the engine enforces them at the seams where writes/exec/external effects happen; any route into a >workspace-only capability requires approval; external effects never fire directly — they queue as pending actions.
tasks.context: Two enforcement layers. (1) Conductor-side: before routing an artifact into a section, conductor.py compares the target section's capability manifest (loaded via sections.py from 3.1) against the route's implied capability; anything beyond workspace-only goes through the approvals file contract — the proven `<app>/approvals/<phase>.ok|.edit|.changes` mechanism in _await_approval (orchestrator.py:6342–6399, verified: decision files cleared on entry, state['awaiting_approval'] set for the GUI, timeout proceeds). (2) Engine-side: the run itself must not exceed the section's declared capabilities — the seams, verified in code: write capability maps to the sandbox flag plumbing (cfg['_allow_writes'] read at orchestrator.py:630 to pick 'workspace-write' vs 'read-only' for codex; resume paths at :639–642 are always workspace-write — a read-only section must therefore refuse sessioned resume, not silently grant writes); external maps to urlfetch.py fetches and any api:/network runner; exec maps to build/verify hooks that run toolchains. Pending actions: a new `<root>/.orchestrator/pending_actions.jsonl` (+ per-action files) where external side-effects (e.g. 5.6 Notion delivery, future integrations) are queued with enough context to execute later upon explicit approval — the M7 exit gate requires 'every external side-effect sat in the pending queue'. Trap: enforcement must be default-deny — a section.json missing the capability block gets workspace-only, with a visible banner, never full trust.

tasks.title: Goal manifest + four-layer termination stack (goal predicate, quiescence, budgets, stall)
tasks.goal: The conductor knows when to stop: a goal manifest defines done (gap report empty + DoD + evalharness threshold); quiescence converts idle cycles into an honest converged-with-open-items report; budgets cap turns/wall-clock/per-provider spend with quota-aware deferral; stall detection (vote_undecided ×2, supersedes oscillation) escalates to the human.
tasks.context: Sub-PR split: (a) goal manifest + goal predicate + quiescence, (b) budgets + stall. Verified mechanisms: the goal predicate composes THREE existing signals — the Documentation gap report (5.2/5.4: empty/thin doc slots emitted as structured gap artifacts; gap report empty = docs complete), DoD checklists (definition_of_done.json, tiered prototype→mvp→v1→production_draft with the binding functionality rule), and evalharness.score_project(app_dir) (evalharness.py:66) ≥ a manifest threshold. Budgets read real spend from costs.py (6.4 — per-turn usage → per-session/section/project meters; plan §10.6: M6 strictly before this, chars are not spend) and integrate with provider pacing state (the engine's _pace_provider/_PACE_LAST, orchestrator.py:1313–1332, paces request rates; the conductor adds day-level quota awareness — Gemini free tier is ~20 req/day/model — deferring routes rather than burning quota). Stall signals, verified: the vote path records state['phase_resolutions'][key]='vote_undecided' (orchestrator.py:6039–6042) — two undecideds in one session = stalled; supersedes oscillation is detectable from 4.3's lineage meta (the same converged/oscillation machinery as 7.2's guards, evaluated globally). Termination layers check in order goal → stall → budget → quiescence each cycle; each termination writes an explicit final report artifact + ledger line — 'converged-with-open-items' must honestly enumerate what is NOT done (§13.2: never fabricate completion). Trap: quiescence must count only non-superseded artifact activity; a lineage churning superseded versions is oscillation (stall), not progress.
subtasks: Sub-PR (a): define goal_manifest.json schema {goal: doc_tier/eval_threshold/custom predicate refs, quiescence_cycles: N, budgets: {turns, wall_clock_s, per_provider: {spend, requests_per_day}}, stall: {vote_undecided_limit: 2}}; load + validate in conductor.py with visible banner on parse failure (safe default: never-terminate-by-goal, still budget-capped).

Implement the goal predicate: gap report empty (query 5.4's gap artifacts via artifacts.py) AND DoD tier items met (definition_of_done.json active tier) AND evalharness.score_project ≥ threshold; each sub-check's pass/fail is recorded individually in the termination report.

Implement quiescence: N consecutive conductor cycles with zero new non-superseded final artifacts → write a converged-with-open-items report artifact enumerating remaining gap items and unmet DoD entries, then stop routing.

Sub-PR (b): implement budget accounting: turns and wall-clock from conductor's own ledger; provider spend/requests from costs.py meters; a route whose target provider is over its daily request quota is DEFERRED (ledgered, retried next cycle) rather than dropped; hard budget exhaustion stops routing and reports.

Implement stall detection: per-session vote_undecided count ≥2 (read from agent_state.json phase_resolutions, orchestrator.py:6039) OR supersedes-chain oscillation (4.3 lineage meta) → escalate: stop routing into the stalled lineage/session, surface an approval-required escalation to the human.
Wire the four layers into the conductor loop in evaluation order goal → stall → budget → quiescence, each cycle, each outcome ledgered with its evidence.

Write termination unit tests: goal-met fixture (all three sub-checks), goal-not-met-by-each-sub-check fixtures, quiescence countdown incl. superseded-churn NOT counting as activity, budget exhaustion + quota deferral, vote_undecided ×2, and the oscillation fixture shared with 7.2.

acceptance_criteria: Goal predicate: terminates ONLY when all three sub-checks pass (gap report empty AND DoD tier met AND score_project ≥ threshold); the termination report shows each sub-check's individual result — a partially-met goal must NOT be reported as 'complete'.

Quiescence: N idle cycles produce a converged-with-open-items report that honestly enumerates remaining gaps and unmet DoD items; superseded-version churn does NOT reset or satisfy the idle counter (it is oscillation, not progress).
Budgets: turns/wall-clock/per-provider spend caps stop routing when exhausted with a ledgered, surfaced reason; spend numbers come from costs.py real accounting, never char counts or estimates.

Quota-aware deferral: a provider at its daily request quota (e.g. Gemini free tier ~20 req/day) causes route DEFERRAL retried next cycle — the route is neither dropped nor executed over-quota; deferral is ledgered.

Every termination/escalation writes an explicit report artifact + ledger line with its evidence; the conductor never just stops silently, and never keeps routing after a termination condition holds.
A corrupt/missing goal manifest yields the safe default (no goal-based termination, budgets still enforced) with a visible banner — never uncapped autonomous running with no budgets.
The overnight loop can always end: with an unreachable goal, EITHER budgets or quiescence terminates the run in bounded time (proven by a test with goal-never-met fixtures).

tasks.title: Oversight dials: full-auto / suggest-only / gated / loops-gated (default) + per-decision undo
tasks.goal: The Conductor exposes four oversight dial positions controlling which routes auto-execute vs. queue for human approval, implemented on the existing approvals file contract, plus per-decision undo: mark an artifact do-not-route, and kill a Conductor-spawned session.
tasks.context: The dial semantics are fixed by the sections plan (orchestrator-v3-sections-plan.md:163-168): full-auto = all routes execute; suggest-only = every route queued as a tappable approval card (the gentle on-ramp); gated = every route needs approval; loops-gated (DEFAULT) = forward routes auto-execute, feedback-loop routes (those 7.2's pre-route guards flag as revisiting an ancestor section via the descendant content-hash / hop-budget metadata) need approval. Reuse the file-contract idiom of `_await_approval` (orchestrator.py:6342): decision files `<key>.ok` / `<key>.changes` dropped into an approvals dir — but keyed by 7.3's deterministic `route_id`, under `<workspace>/.conductor/approvals/`, and NON-blocking: the Conductor loop must keep draining other routes while some pend (unlike `_await_approval`'s blocking poll). Undo "kill spawned session" reuses the stop machinery: GUI `stopRun` already does liveness-checked SIGTERM→5s→SIGKILL via the lock-file pid (gui/Sources/OrchestratorGUI/OrchestratorStore.swift:3307-3342); 7.0 extends coverage to Conductor-minted runs. Trap: 7.4's invariant — a route into a section whose capability manifest exceeds workspace-only ALWAYS requires approval — must hold on every dial including full-auto; the dial can only make oversight stricter, never bypass 7.4. conductor.py does not exist yet; it is created by 7.1 (this card extends it).
subtasks: In conductor.py, add `oversight` to conductor_state.json: {dial: "full_auto"|"suggest_only"|"gated"|"loops_gated"}, default loops_gated; read at loop start, re-read on state-file mtime change so the GUI can flip the dial mid-run.

In conductor.py's route-execution step (after 7.2's guards decide a route and 7.3 computes route_id), add `classify_route(route, dial) -> "auto"|"needs_approval"`: loops_gated consults the loop-guard metadata (route target already in artifact's lineage chain) to distinguish forward vs feedback routes; 7.4's capability check overrides to needs_approval on every dial.

Implement the pending-route contract: write `<workspace>/.conductor/approvals/<route_id>.pending` (JSON: artifact, target section, rule, human-readable reason) atomically; the Conductor polls for `<route_id>.ok` (approve) / `<route_id>.changes` (reject, body = optional reason) each wake, consumes the decision file, appends the decision to the routing ledger, and executes or drops the route. Pending routes never block draining of other routes.

tasks.title: Workspace snapshots: git commits at quiescence points + before routing waves; roll back the night
tasks.goal: The workspace is a git repo; the Conductor commits at every quiescence point and before every routing wave, tagging each commit with the routing-ledger cursor, so "roll back the night" = git reset to a tag + ledger truncation/replay.
tasks.context: This is gap #4 from the adversarial pass (orchestrator-v3-sections-plan.md:350-355): whole-run rollback, free offsite backup, and the substrate that makes 7.10's replay scrub real. Reuse the engine's proven git plumbing rather than writing new subprocess code: `_git(dir, *args)` (orchestrator.py:4221) runs git via procutil with process-group timeout kill; `_ensure_workspace_gitignore(root)` (orchestrator.py:4274) already manages `<root>/.gitignore` and excludes `.orchestrator_runtime/`; `ensure_build_repo` (orchestrator.py:4304) is the idempotent init idiom (init + gitignore + empty root commit). DRIFT NOTE vs the plan: the workspace may ALREADY be a git repo — `_ensure_workspace_gitignore`'s docstring says the factory `run.sh` may `git add -A` + commit at workspace level — so snapshot code must compose with an existing history and existing gitignore rules (append-only-missing idiom), never re-init or clobber. The ledger cursor is the byte offset (or line count) of the routing ledger JSONL from 7.1; embed it in the tag name/message so reset and ledger truncation stay in lockstep. Rollback must not yank state out from under live sessions: stop Conductor-minted runs first via 7.0's stop coverage. docsync.py (5.5) renders docs into a per-project worktree; snapshots must not commit its worktree internals or fight its bot-identity commits.
subtasks: In conductor.py, add `ensure_workspace_repo(root)`: if `<root>/.git` missing, init + `_ensure_workspace_gitignore(root)` + empty root commit (mirror ensure_build_repo, orchestrator.py:4304); if present, only append missing gitignore rules. Extend _WORKSPACE_GITIGNORE_RULES (orchestrator.py:4274) with Conductor scratch: `.conductor/approvals/`, `*.lock`, `.orch-locks/`, `.stream/`.

Add `snapshot(root, reason, ledger_cursor)`: `_git` add -A + commit with a structured message (`conductor-snapshot: <reason> cursor=<n> ts=<iso>`) + annotated tag `conductor/<ts>-<cursor>`; no-op cleanly (return the prior tag) when the tree is clean; never raises — a failed snapshot is ledger-logged and the run continues (snapshots are safety, not a gate).

Call snapshot() from the Conductor loop at the two mandated points: (a) immediately BEFORE executing a routing wave (batch of routes fired in one wake), (b) at each quiescence point detected by 7.5's termination stack.

Implement `rollback(root, tag)`: refuse if any Conductor-minted session is live (offer/perform stop via 7.0's run.pid + lock machinery first); `git reset --hard <tag>`; truncate the routing ledger JSONL to the cursor encoded in the tag; rewrite conductor_state.json's derived cursors by replaying the truncated ledger (the same scan-and-dedup path 7.3's restart uses).

Expose rollback as a CLI verb on conductor.py (`--rollback <tag>` and `--rollback-last-night` choosing the newest tag before a given timestamp) with a dry-run mode that prints the diffstat and the sessions that would be stopped.
Coordinate with docsync.py: the per-project doc worktree (5.5) is external to the workspace snapshot; assert its path is gitignored so snapshots and bot commits never interleave.
Write the rollback integration test (see test plan); run `make verify`.
acceptance_criteria: A workspace that is not yet a git repo is initialized idempotently; a workspace that already IS a git repo (run.sh factory flow) keeps its history and its extra gitignore rules — only missing managed rules are appended, matching the existing append-only-missing idiom.

Every routing wave is preceded by a snapshot commit+tag, and every quiescence point produces one; each tag encodes the routing-ledger cursor; a clean tree produces no empty commit and no duplicate tag.

Snapshot failure (git missing, disk full, index.lock held) never crashes or stalls the Conductor loop: the failure is ledger-logged with the git stderr, a visible event is emitted, and routing continues.
Locks, `.stream/` NDJSON, `.conductor/approvals/`, and `.orchestrator_runtime/` never appear in any snapshot commit (gitignore-enforced).
Rollback with a live Conductor-minted session running refuses (or stops the session via liveness-checked SIGTERM→SIGKILL) — it never resets files out from under a writing process.

After `rollback(tag)`: the working tree equals the tagged snapshot, the routing ledger is truncated exactly to the tag's cursor, and a restarted Conductor neither re-fires routes that were undone nor skips routes that are now legitimately pending again — replay state derives solely from the truncated ledger.
Rolling back does not delete tags after the cursor (the rolled-back-over history remains inspectable in git); a second rollback to an earlier tag also works.
Dry-run rollback mutates nothing (verified by diffing tree + ledger before/after) while printing an accurate diffstat.
All git invocations go through `_git`/procutil with timeouts — no bare subprocess calls that can deadlock on a hung credential helper.
test_plan: tests/test_conductor_snapshots.py::test_rollback_integration — the plan's gate: seed a temp workspace, run a scripted sequence (snapshot → route wave → artifacts written → snapshot → more routes), roll back to the middle tag, assert tree + ledger cursor + replayed conductor_state all match the tagged moment (integration test).

tasks.goal: The GUI's events consumer posts macOS notifications when the Conductor needs approval, stalls, converges, or exhausts a budget — batched during configurable quiet hours so an overnight run never pings at 1am, and summarized when quiet hours end.

tasks.context: The architectural insight to preserve (orchestrator-v3-sections-plan.md:240-256): a pipeline is NOT a new engine construct — it is a saved preset of Conductor routing rules plus a goal manifest, so it inherits Mission Control, budgets, oversight dials, replay, and termination for free; there is no second execution engine. Keep the two workflow layers distinct: within-section workflows (phase JSON inside one session) vs cross-section pipelines (routing presets) — one format spanning both would re-entangle what the architecture separated. GUI precedents, all verified: `RunProfile` (gui/Sources/OrchestratorGUI/ModelLibrary.swift:288) with `listProfiles()` (OrchestratorStore.swift:1450), `saveProfile` (snapshot-to-named-JSON with slugified filename, atomic write), and `applyProfile` (:1493, materialize-onto-project) — pipeline presets follow this exact directory-of-JSON pattern in a sibling presets dir; `WorkflowBuilderSheet` (WorkflowBuilder.swift:21) is the sheet-based editor precedent; RoutingGridView's "the grid IS the file" single-source-of-truth discipline (RoutingGridView.swift:5-14) applies: the canvas IS the compiled JSON, no divergent in-memory model. Engine side: conductor.py gets a preset loader that overlays the preset's routing rules + goal manifest for the run. The round-trip gate (canvas→JSON→canvas lossless) forces the compiled JSON to carry everything the canvas needs, including node positions — put layout in a `"ui"` sub-object the Conductor ignores.

Machine-readable steps parse via schemas.extract_structured_blocks (schemas.py:139) — no new parser. The activity append contract copies mistakes.py exactly (mistakes.py:85–134: one O_APPEND line under 3500B, schemas.redact_secrets on strings, never raises). Plan-step citation threads through 4.4's delegation.json into publish meta; intent staleness rides 4.3's supersedes machinery and 4.9's badge surface. Gate placement in conductor.py: before executing any multi-step intent (a 7.2 custom chain or goal decomposition spanning >1 route), publish the plan artifact, ledger it, and classify it against 7.6's dial exactly like a route: full_auto → execute immediately (the plan is still published + ledgered — the trace exists even ungated); suggest_only and gated → pend for approval; loops_gated → pend iff any step targets a section already in the driving artifact's lineage (the same feedback-loop metadata 7.2's guards read); 7.4's capability override forces pending on EVERY dial for plans containing steps into >workspace-only sections.

Pending-plan contract: write <workspace>/.conductor/approvals/<plan_id>.pending atomically (JSON: plan artifact id/version, step summary, reason); decisions are <plan_id>.ok (execute as-is), <plan_id>.changes (drop, body = reason, ledgered), and <plan_id>.edit — the .edit BODY becomes plan v(n+1) via 4.3's supersedes path (by=human recorded), and v(n+1)'s steps are what the executor reads; pending plans never block other Conductor work (7.6's non-blocking discipline) and survive restart (rediscovered from the approvals dir + ledger, 7.3-style).

Execution + activity trace: as the Conductor executes approved plan steps (minting/routing via 4.4/7.2), append one line per step transition to <workspace>/.conductor/activity.jsonl AND to the executing session's <session>/activity.jsonl: {ts, plan_id, plan_version, step_id, actor, action, status: started|completed|failed, artifact_ids[]} — written with mistakes.py's exact append contract (single O_APPEND line, <3500B, redact_secrets, never raises; mistakes.py:85–134); crash-resume must not duplicate step lines (dedup on {plan_id, plan_version, step_id, status} via the 7.3 ledger-scan idiom).

tasks.title: (radar adopt) Failure artifacts: terminal failures emit a typed, routable `failure` artifact — never a bare "run failed"
tasks.goal: Every terminal failure — agent-ladder/circuit-breaker exhaustion, config abort, release-gate repair-budget exhaustion, hard crash, Conductor budget exhaustion, stall — publishes a typed `failure` artifact {error_class, message, last_checkpoint, cost_spent, events_cursor, source_session} through artifacts.py, final-on-publish, routed via routing presets to notifications or a Fixer persona session. Failures become diagnosable, routable events instead of dead ends.
tasks.context: Radar ADOPT NOW #4 (designated error handler pattern). Engine terminal paths verified: AgentError → run_finished status='aborted' (orchestrator.py:7548–7555) — this is where circuit-breaker/fallback-ladder exhaustion lands (call_agent re-raises after the 'exhausted' event at :1278–1279; a fully output-less phase raises at :5757–5759); AppError → status='skipped' (:7556–7562); release-gate repair-budget exhaustion leaves state error 'release gate: …' (:6853) with only an emit at :6903–6906. Critical gap found while verifying: a hard CRASH today emits NOTHING — process_app (:6448) has no generic except, run_once merely logs 'unexpected worker failure' (:7927–7928), and the app shows 'running' until the 5400s stale heuristic (_is_stale_running_state, :324). So the 'crash' class requires adding a process_app except-Exception wrapper emitting run_finished status='crashed' (a new status string, not a new event kind; the GUI already treats any non-done run_finished as failure, EngineEvents.swift:35). last_checkpoint comes from agent_state.json (current_phase/current_round/completed_phases, load_state :2622); cost_spent from 6.4's costs.py meters; Conductor-side classes (budget_exhausted, stalled) hook 7.5's termination stack and route through 7.2's rules, whose pre-route hop/depth guards (reading 4.3's lineage meta) are the loop brake against infinite Fixer chains. No drift from the plan beyond the crash-path gap above.
