tasks.context: OrchestratorStore.swift (verified 3,456 lines today) owns everything: fleet scan — refresh() at :823 with refreshInFlight/refreshPending coalescing, refreshGeneration watchdog at :829–:847 and the stale-generation guard at :901–:906 (plan said :823–:897; the machinery actually runs through ~:909 — trust the code); the single 1.5s Timer at :786; discovery via BackgroundProjectLoader.discoverApps (defined :8, called :866); run control — stopProject :3072–:3097 and stopRun :3307–:3342 with SIGTERM→SIGKILL escalation and .orch-locks/<name>.lock cleanup at :3312; chat state — chatMessages didSet :628–:629 → saveChatHistory (~:2951); local-model/agent probes — refreshLocalModels :780, probeAgentVersions :1693–:1713. By 8.1 time the store also carries M1 chat lifecycle (1.4/1.5/1.6), 3.0 nested discovery, and 7.0 pid-file stop. gui/Tests/OrchestratorGUITests today holds only logic tests (EngineLogicTests, TranscriptParserTests, StyleGuardTests, …) — task 2.7's golden-path UI suite for the store is the HARD prerequisite; do not start until it is green. Deliver as three sub-PRs (the 3×M), each a pure extraction with zero behavior change, plan mode first per plan §11. Trap: the generation/watchdog semantics (late background completion must never clobber fresher state) are load-bearing and easy to break when moving scan results into per-session objects.
subtasks: Inventory pass (no code motion): classify every @Published property and method of OrchestratorStore.swift into fleet-scoped / session-scoped / shared-service buckets; record the map in a doc comment or gui/DESIGN note in the first sub-PR.
Confirm the 2.7 UI suite is green on the unmodified store (make gui-test); this is the before-snapshot for every extraction.

Sub-PR (a): extract SessionModel — per-session run status, transcript-tail state, per-chat history (the 1.4 per-chat keys), stream state — as an ObservableObject the store owns in a [name: SessionModel] dictionary; forward legacy @Published surfaces during transition so views migrate incrementally.

Sub-PR (b): extract the scanning service — the refresh() body (BackgroundConfigLoader/BackgroundProjectLoader/FactoryScanner/EventsScanner calls at :857–:900) behind a FleetScanner type; the store keeps ownership of refreshInFlight/refreshGeneration watchdog semantics unchanged, applying snapshots to fleet state and routing per-session slices into SessionModel objects.

Sub-PR (c): extract run control — launch (Process spawn paths), stopProject :3072 / stopRun :3307, lock and pid-file handling — into a RunController used by SessionModel; keep SIGTERM→SIGKILL grace timing and lock-cleanup order byte-for-byte in behavior.
After each sub-PR: run the full 2.7 UI suite + existing logic tests + StyleGuard; commit only when green; never batch two extractions in one PR.
Mechanically retarget existing tests that referenced moved members; add no new behavior.
acceptance_criteria: The 2.7 golden-path UI suite passes on the unmodified store, and again after EVERY sub-PR — a red suite blocks the next extraction.
Zero user-visible behavior change: launch/stop, refresh cadence, watchdog recovery, chat lifecycle, and lock cleanup behave identically before and after.
The refreshGeneration guard still holds: a late completion from an abandoned scan never overwrites state from a newer refresh (test simulates a stalled scan).
stopRun/stopProject still verify pid liveness before signaling (never SIGTERM a stranger) and still clean .orch-locks/<name>.lock after SIGKILL escalation.
Per-session state (run status, chat history, transcript tail) lives on SessionModel, not in name-keyed global dictionaries, for every migrated surface.
No sub-PR mixes extraction with a behavior change or a new feature; diffs are reviewable as pure moves plus forwarding shims.
make gui-build and make gui-test pass; StyleGuard (ci_style_check.sh / StyleGuardTests) stays green.
The app must NOT regress the one-timer invariant (start() guard at :785): reopening the window still never stacks a second refresh timer.
test_plan: Gate (from plan): UI tests green before/after each extraction — run make gui-test on the unmodified store, then after sub-PRs (a), (b), (c).
Extend the 2.7 suite with a stale-generation test: start refresh, force the 20s watchdog recovery, deliver the late result, assert newer state wins.
Kill/stop test: launch a fake run, stopRun, assert lock removed and no signal sent to a recycled pid.

tasks.title: Pane canvas: drag-in split (2–3 max) + relaxed background polling + mtime-cached focused scan
tasks.goal: Replace the single-selection center pane with a pane canvas — one pane full-width by default, drag a second/third chat in to split, overflow strip beyond three — and make polling economics honest: focused panes fast, background sessions relaxed, focused scans skipped when files haven't changed.
tasks.context: Today the shell is single-selection: AppShellView holds @State selection: ShellSelection? (:26) and derives selectedProject (:85); one detail pane, one inspector (ShellInspectorPane :129). The store polls everything at one cadence — the single 1.5s Timer (OrchestratorStore.swift:786) drives a full-fleet refresh(); 1.10 already made the FOCUSED cadence 500ms as a parameter but explicitly deferred the scan-machinery work here. The mtime-caching precedent already exists: EventsScanner.scan re-reads only files whose mtime/size moved (comment at :884–:886) — extend that pattern to the per-project transcript/state scan (BackgroundProjectLoader.loadProjects, called at :867) so a 500ms focused tick that finds unchanged mtimes does no parse work. After 8.1, each pane binds a SessionModel, which is what makes per-pane cadence tractable — build this on the split store. Product spec: sections-plan §8.3 ("pane canvas replaces single selection — one pane full-width by default, drag a second chat in to split (2–3 max, overflow strip)") and §10 shell layout. Trap: background sessions must still surface state changes (run finished, approval needed) within a few seconds — relaxed ≠ frozen; and the energy check is a real gate, not prose.
subtasks: Define PaneCanvasState (ordered pane list of session ids, focused pane id, overflow list) on the fleet store; cap panes at 3 with overflow strip entries beyond that.

Build PaneCanvasView replacing the single detail region in AppShellView: 1 pane full-width default; 2–3 panes split with draggable dividers; overflow strip renders compact chips that swap into a pane on click.

Implement drag-in: chats in the left rail become draggable (onDrag with the session id); PaneCanvasView accepts onDrop to open-as-split; dropping onto an existing pane replaces its content; StyleGuard-clean visuals via ThemeTokens.
Wire per-pane cadence: focused pane ticks at 500ms (1.10's parameter), non-focused visible panes at 1.5s, background (no pane) sessions relaxed to ~5s; single scheduling point, no timer per pane.

Add mtime+size short-circuit to the focused-scan path: cache (path → mtime,size,parse) for transcript/events/state files per SessionModel; unchanged stat = zero re-read/re-parse (mirror EventsScanner's cache).
Keyboard/⌘K integration: 'focus pane 1/2/3' and close-pane verbs registered in the existing command palette (ContentView.swift filteredCommands).
Run the energy check: 3 live sessions, 2 panes, measure CPU with the mtime cache on vs off; record numbers in the PR.
acceptance_criteria: Default state is exactly one full-width pane; dragging a second chat in splits; a fourth chat lands in the overflow strip, never a fourth pane.
Closing a pane returns cleanly to the wider layout; the focused pane is always visually identifiable; focus follows click.
Focused pane updates at 500ms; a background session's completed run still surfaces in the rail/status within 5s — relaxed polling must NOT hide state changes indefinitely.
With all watched files unchanged (stable mtime+size), a focused tick performs no file reads or parses (assert via instrumented counter in tests).
A changed file with same mtime but different size is still detected (cache keys on mtime AND size).
No layout clipping at min window size — panes reflow or collapse to the overflow strip, never truncate content silently.
CPU/energy on a 3-session, 2-pane run is measured and not worse than the pre-8.2 single-pane baseline; numbers in the PR description.
StyleGuard (ci_style_check.sh + StyleGuardTests) green; no rogue colors/fonts in the new views.
test_plan: Gate (from plan): StyleGuard + energy check.
gui/Tests: PaneCanvasState logic tests — add/drop/replace/overflow/focus transitions; cap-at-3 invariant.
gui/Tests: mtime-cache test — instrumented scanner counter proves zero parses on unchanged stats, and detects a same-mtime/different-size write.

rules: R5 resizing must cause reflow, not clipping — panes and overflow strip at min window size

tasks.title: Privacy tiering: sensitivity field enforced at resolve_runner + build_context; sensitive fallback terminates at local
tasks.goal: Add a sensitivity field at project and artifact level, enforce it mechanically at the two seams everything passes through (resolve_runner and build_context), make sensitive fallback chains terminate at local models, and ship a per-project "Private (local models only)" toggle.
tasks.context: Sections-plan §11 gap #7. The two enforcement seams are verified: resolve_runner (orchestrator.py:1004) is the single chokepoint returning a runner callable for any agent id — cloud runners are codex/claude/gemini in RUNNERS (:1000) plus M6's api:* runners; local is local:<model>/ollama (modelrouting._is_local, modelrouting.py:291, is the existing local/cloud classifier — reuse it, don't write a second one). build_context (orchestrator.py:1791) gained 4.7's artifact-retrieval layer with an explicit sensitivity filter STUB — this task implements it. Fallback: call_agent's ladder (:1194) walks _fallback_steps (:1108) built from modelrouting.fallback_chain (:329) + the cloud→local net (_local_fallback_model :1088); for a sensitive session every step must be local, so filter the chain at assembly, not at failure time. Sensitivity lives in artifact meta.json (4.1 store) and at project level (project config/agent_state). Doctrine from QUALITY_RULES.md: gated beats prompted — enforcement is a mock-runner test proving sensitive content never reaches a cloud callable, not a prompt line. Failure semantics matter: a sensitive session whose roster resolves to zero local runners must fail loudly with a visible banner, never silently proceed on cloud.
subtasks: Schema: add `sensitivity` ("normal" | "private") to artifact meta.json (artifacts.py registry validation) and a project-level flag read into cfg at run start; document precedence (project private ⇒ all its sessions/artifacts treated private).

Enforcement point 1 — resolve_runner (orchestrator.py:1004): when the session/project is private, resolving a non-local agent id raises a typed PrivacyViolation instead of returning the runner; roster assembly maps cloud ids to local equivalents up front so normal operation never hits the raise.

Enforcement point 2 — _fallback_steps (orchestrator.py:1108): for private sessions filter every chain step through modelrouting._is_local; the cloud→local net remains as the terminal step; empty local roster ⇒ loud failure + visible banner event, not silent cloud fallback.

Enforcement point 3 — build_context (orchestrator.py:1791): implement 4.7's sensitivity filter — private artifacts are excluded from retrieval into any session that could run on a cloud runner; private sessions may pull anything.
Also gate the 4.4/7.2 routing surface: a private artifact routed to a section whose session would use cloud runners is blocked with a surfaced reason (Conductor reads the same predicate).

GUI: "Private (local models only)" toggle per project (Configuration/inspector surface), state shown honestly — the toggle reflects enforced state, with a badge on the session header; StyleGuard-clean.
Emit a privacy_enforced/privacy_blocked event (events.py KINDS) whenever enforcement rewrites a roster or blocks a route, so the ledger explains every substitution.
acceptance_criteria: The enforcement test passes: with a mock cloud runner installed in RUNNERS, a private session's full lifecycle (turns, fallback exhaustion, context build, routing) never invokes the mock with any content — asserted by the mock recording zero calls.
Private fallback chains contain only local steps end-to-end; a chain configured with cloud rescue steps is filtered at assembly and the filtering is visible in events, not silent.
A private session with zero installed local models fails loudly before the first turn (visible banner + clear error naming the fix), and must NOT silently fall back to any cloud runner.
Private artifacts never appear in build_context retrieval for non-private sessions; normal artifacts remain retrievable everywhere (no over-blocking).

The GUI toggle reflects real enforced state (R2): toggling private on a project with cloud-only roster surfaces the conflict immediately rather than pretending privacy while cloud runners remain resolvable.
Sensitivity survives crash/resume: a resumed private session re-derives the same enforcement (flag read from persisted state, not in-memory only).
Existing non-private behavior is byte-identical: golden transcript suite green; no performance regression in resolve_runner's hot path.
Turning the toggle OFF does not retroactively leak: artifacts already marked private keep their own sensitivity.
test_plan: Gate (from plan): enforcement test — local-only content never reaches a cloud runner (mock); tests/ mock-runner fixture asserting zero cloud invocations across turn, fallback, pull, and route paths.
Chain-filter unit tests on _fallback_steps with mixed chains; empty-local-roster loud-failure test.
build_context exclusion test with fixture artifacts of both sensitivities in both session types (4-cell matrix).
Crash-resume test: kill a private session mid-round, resume, re-assert mock records zero calls. Golden suite + make verify.
rules: §9.3 collect only necessary data / §9 privacy — sensitive material never leaves the machine; enforcement is mechanical, not prompted (QUALITY_RULES gated-vs-prompted doctrine)
R2 interface must never lie — the Private toggle reflects enforced reality; conflicts surface immediately
§13.5 AI output should not directly perform destructive/boundary-crossing actions — routing a private artifact to a cloud-capable section is blocked, not warned

tasks.title: Lifecycle/GC: tombstone superseded artifacts, exclude killed lineages, --gc dry-run, archive-project verb
tasks.goal: Give the artifact store a data lifecycle: superseded artifacts beyond N versions become tombstones, killed lineages disappear from pull/search, `--gc` previews before it touches anything, and a whole project can be archived with one verb.
tasks.context: Sections-plan §11 gap #11. Operates entirely on M4's store: artifacts.py (4.1) with meta.json {id, type, version, supersedes, lineage[], content_hash, status}; 4.3's supersedes chains and lineage depth/hop fields; consumers are 4.7's build_context retrieval layer and 2.6's search.py FTS5 index. Kill/park decisions originate in Ideas (sections-plan §2 item 1: "kill/park decisions so dead ideas don't resurface") — a killed lineage is one whose head artifact carries status "killed". Design decisions to hold: tombstoning removes body.md but PRESERVES meta.json (lineage/provenance chains must never break — a consumer holding a stale reference gets an honest "tombstoned" answer, not a missing file); GC never touches the latest final of any live lineage regardless of N; `--gc` is dry-run BY DefAULT printing a diff-style report (counts, ids, bytes reclaimed), with an explicit --apply flag to act — mirroring the repo's dry-run-diff culture (5.6, 8.8, 3.0 migration). "Archive project" moves the project dir to an archive/ area and drops it from discovery/search/pull without deleting anything. N is configurable (config.yaml runtime key), default documented.
subtasks: artifacts.py: add tombstone(artifact_id) — replaces body.md with a stub, sets meta status "tombstoned", preserves all meta/lineage fields; resolver answers tombstoned reads with a typed honest error.

artifacts.py: gc_plan(workspace, keep_versions=N) — walk supersedes chains; select tombstone candidates (superseded depth > N, not lineage head, not referenced by an unreconciled branch per 4.3); return a structured plan (ids, bytes, reasons).
CLI: `--gc` prints the plan as a readable diff report and exits 0 without modifying anything; `--gc --apply` executes the plan and emits one artifact-lifecycle event per tombstone.

Exclusion: build_context retrieval (4.7 layer) and search.py indexing/query skip artifacts with status killed or tombstoned, and every artifact in a lineage whose head is killed; reindex (`--reindex`) purges already-indexed dead entries.

Archive-project verb: engine helper moves workspace/<project> to workspace/.archive/<project> (refusing while any lock in .orch-locks names its sessions), drops it from find_apps discovery and GUI discovery; GUI menu action + confirmation naming exactly what happens.
Config: runtime.gc_keep_versions (default e.g. 5) in config.yaml, read via cget; document in the file's _docs.
Unarchive path: moving the dir back restores full function (test proves round-trip).
acceptance_criteria: `--gc` with no flags NEVER modifies any file — verified by a before/after tree hash in the test; the printed plan names every candidate with id, reason, and bytes.
`--gc --apply` tombstones exactly the planned set; meta.json and lineage chains remain intact and traversable across tombstones.
The latest final artifact of every live lineage is never a GC candidate, regardless of keep_versions.
Killed lineages return zero results from both build_context retrieval and FTS5 search, including content indexed before the kill (after reindex).
Reading a tombstoned artifact yields a typed, honest 'tombstoned' response with surviving meta — never a raw missing-file error surfaced to the user (§5.3).
Archive refuses (with a clear message) while any session of the project holds a live lock; after archive, the project vanishes from GUI discovery and engine find_apps; unarchive restores it fully.
Archive/GC never hard-delete: no code path in this task unlinks meta.json or removes a project dir permanently.
GC is crash-safe: killing --gc --apply mid-plan leaves every artifact either fully tombstoned or untouched (per-artifact atomicity), and a re-run completes the remainder without double-reporting.
test_plan: Gate (from plan): GC dry-run diff test — fixture store with deep supersedes chains; assert plan contents and zero mutation on dry-run, exact planned mutation on --apply.
Exclusion tests: killed-lineage fixture invisible to retrieve and search; reindex purge test.
Tombstone-read test (typed error, meta preserved); lineage-traversal-across-tombstone test.
Archive round-trip test incl. locked-project refusal; crash-kill test mid --apply. make verify.
rules: §6.4 deletion must have clear semantics — tombstone vs archive vs never-hard-delete is the explicit model
§6.2 never silently discard data — dry-run by default, explicit --apply, meta always preserved
§5.3 errors must not expose internals — tombstoned reads answer honestly, not with a stack trace
repo: dry-run diff culture (5.6 Notion exporter, 8.8 migrator precedent); repo: golden transcript suite green (retrieval changes must not alter live-session bytes)
out_of_scope: Hard deletion or disk-space quotas — GC only tombstones
Time-based retention policies (version-count based only, per plan)

tasks.title: Config migration: one-shot migrator with dry-run diff for tuned workflows, phase_rules, model_routing → section manifests
tasks.goal: Ship migrate_v3.py: a one-shot, idempotent migrator that maps a user's tuned V2 fleet configs (workflows/*.json, phase_rules.json, model_routing.json) into V3 section manifests, dry-run diff by default, losing nothing silently.
tasks.context: Users have hand-tuned three fleet files whose shapes are verified in-repo: workflows/*.json (14 files today; seeded by workflows.ensure_seeded :678, loaded by load_workflow :693 — disk wins over seeds, so tuned copies differ from V3 section seeds); phase_rules.json ({schema_version, global_app_rules[], phases{<key>: {rules, required_output, acceptance_checks}}} — phase_rules.load_rules :46); model_routing.json ({enabled, fallback{cloud_to_local, local_model, chains{}}, phases{<key>: {claude/codex/gemini/ollama, *_reasoning, timeout, agents}}} — modelrouting.load_routing :121, per-app overlay load_routing_for_app :222). V3 targets: sections/<name>/section.json workflow (3.1), section-scoped rules (3.2 lookup order section → project-override → global), per-section roles/routing overlays (3.4). Workspace DIR migration already happened in 3.0 — explicitly out of scope. Mapping policy: a tuned workflow maps to the section seeded from it (brainstorm→ideas, research→research, audit→qa, app_spec→planning, library_mining→library, build family→build); phase-keyed rules/routing entries follow their phase's owning section; global_app_rules stay global unless 8.4 moved them to Build (coordinate with 8.4's manifest schema). Anything unmappable is REPORTED, never dropped. Migrator writes nothing without --apply; --apply backs up originals first.
subtasks: migrate_v3.py skeleton: stdlib-only CLI (`python3 migrate_v3.py [--apply] [--workspace PATH]`); default mode scans, computes the full plan, prints a unified-diff-style report per target file, exits 0 with zero writes.

Diff engine: for each source file, compare against its pristine seed (workflows.ensure_seeded content, shipped phase_rules/model_routing seeds) to isolate USER TUNING — only tuned deltas migrate; untouched seeds are reported as 'no tuning, section seed wins'.

Workflow mapper: tuned workflows/*.json deltas → the owning section's section.json workflow block, using the 3.6/8.3 seed-source table; unknown/custom workflows map to a generated custom section stub (flagged in the report for review, still data-complete).
Rules mapper: phase_rules.json phases{} entries → owning section's scoped rules file keyed per 3.2; global_app_rules routed per 8.4's home (Build manifest for iOS items, global for neutral items).

Routing mapper: model_routing.json phases{} entries → owning section's routing overlay (3.4 merge layers); fallback{} block stays fleet-level; per-app model_routing.json overlays (load_routing_for_app :222) are detected and reported but left in place (still honored by the overlay merge).
--apply: write targets atomically (temp+rename), back up each modified/superseded original to <file>.v2.bak with a manifest of what moved where; never delete sources.

Idempotency + completion marker: record a migration receipt (e.g. .orch-migrated-v3.json with source hashes); re-running detects it and reports 'already migrated' (or re-diffs against new tuning) instead of double-applying.

Unmappable-key handling: every key the mapper doesn't recognize appears in a loud UNMAPPED section of the report and blocks --apply unless --allow-unmapped is passed (which still preserves them in the .bak + receipt).
acceptance_criteria: Default (no --apply) run performs ZERO writes — proven by before/after tree hash in tests — and prints a complete plan: every tuned delta, its destination, and every unmapped key.

--apply produces section manifests that load cleanly via the 3.1 loader and --lint-section, and a session run in a migrated section uses the tuned values (verified end-to-end on a fixture: a tuned phase rule appears in the rendered playbook post-migration).
No tuned data is silently lost: every source key is either migrated, explicitly reported as seed-identical, or listed as UNMAPPED; unmapped keys block --apply by default.
Originals survive: sources are backed up to .v2.bak with a what-moved-where manifest; nothing is deleted.
Idempotent: a second run after --apply is a no-op with an 'already migrated' report; it must NOT duplicate rules/routing entries or re-append to section files.
Crash-safe: killing --apply mid-run leaves each target file either fully written (atomic rename) or absent; re-run completes the remainder.
Per-app model_routing.json overlays keep working unmodified after migration (overlay merge test), and workspace directory layout is untouched (3.0 owns that).
The migrated fleet passes make verify and the golden transcript suite: engine behavior with migrated manifests matches the tuned-V2 behavior for a representative workflow.
test_plan: Gate (from plan): migrator tests on copies of real configs — fixture set containing (a) pristine seeds, (b) this repo's actual phase_rules.json/model_routing.json/workflows copied verbatim, (c) a synthetically tuned trio; assert plan contents, zero-write dry-run, apply results, and idempotent re-run for all three.
Behavior-parity test: run one workflow pre-migration (tuned V2 files) and post-migration (section manifests), assert the rendered phase playbook and routing resolution are equivalent.
Crash-kill test: interrupt --apply between targets; re-run; assert completion without duplication.
Unmapped-key fixture blocks --apply and lists the key. make verify + golden suite.

tasks.title: Local-model JIT lifecycle, basic: per-request keep_alive, LRU evict on load, runtime/loaded_models.json ledger, per-section pins
tasks.goal: run_local requests carry an explicit keep_alive; before any model load, an LRU eviction pass frees unified memory down to a configured budget (pinned models exempt); a flock-guarded runtime/loaded_models.json ledger records what is resident and when it was last used; sections can pin models via their manifest — so 11 sections can share one Mac's unified memory overnight without beachballing, and every degradation is a visible banner.
tasks.context: Radar ADOPT NOW #8 (LM Studio's JIT loading + TTL auto-unload — 'required for V3's own promise'). Verified substrate: run_local (orchestrator.py:962) POSTs {model, prompt, stream:false} (+optional think, :978–980) to Ollama's /api/generate (:970) — NO keep_alive today, so Ollama's daemon default governs residency and 11 sections' models pile up. localmodels.py is the charter module ('everything local-model'): server_running (:233) probes OLLAMA_TAGS_URL (:40); total_ram_gb (:90) gives the memory ceiling; load_registry (:67) yields curated size_gb per model (local_models.json); installed_models_cached (:151). Real Ollama capabilities (verify against current docs, per the repo's 'real capability, not invented' discipline — see :972): /api/generate accepts keep_alive ('5m', 0 = unload after response, -1 = resident indefinitely); GET /api/ps lists loaded models with size and expiry; an empty-prompt generate with keep_alive:0 unloads a model. The roster 'ollama' agent (run_ollama :924) shells out to the CLI and is OUT of scope — mirror the ollama_reasoning accepted-but-noop warn-once precedent (:941–950). Concurrency: multiple engine processes run overnight, so the ledger needs an advisory flock (acquire_app_lock precedent, orchestrator.py:374); /api/ps is ground truth, the ledger adds last_used history + pins. Constraint: no new cfg["_…"] keys (2.3 grep gate) — policy is read from config/section manifests, not stashed per-turn in cfg.
subtasks: localmodels.py: add OLLAMA_PS_URL + loaded_models_ps(timeout) — never-raising probe (server_running pattern, :233) returning [{model, size_bytes, expires_at}]; and unload_model(model) via empty-prompt /api/generate with keep_alive:0, best-effort with explicit ok/False result.

Ledger: read_ledger/write_ledger for runtime/loaded_models.json (runtime/ created beside the engine; add to .gitignore) — entries {model, last_used_ts, size_gb, pinned_by:[section]}, whole-file flock (fcntl) around read-modify-write; on read, reconcile against /api/ps (ps wins on residency; ledger contributes last_used + pins); corrupt ledger → rebuild from /api/ps with a visible warning, never crash.

ensure_capacity(model, budget_gb, pins, on_warn): resolve the incoming model's size (registry size_gb → /api/ps size → conservative default WITH warning); while resident_total + incoming > budget_gb, unload the least-recently-used non-pinned model; every eviction and every failure is reported via on_warn; returns the action list for logging (§17).

run_local integration (orchestrator.py:962): before the POST, call ensure_capacity with the resolved budget and active pins; add keep_alive to the request body — pinned model → the configured pin duration (default -1), otherwise models.local_keep_alive (config.yaml scalar, default '5m'); after the response, update the ledger's last_used under flock. Budget default: models.local_memory_budget_gb, falling back to a fixed fraction of total_ram_gb (localmodels.py:90). NO new cfg["_…"] keys — read config via cget, pass values as arguments.

Per-section pins: sections/<name>/section.json gains optional local_pins: ["model:tag"] (3.1 loader validates: must be a list of strings, unknown/uninstalled tags warn visibly and are ignored); the engine resolves the running section's pins into ensure_capacity's pin set; pinned models are never LRU-evicted and get the pin keep_alive.

Degradation banners (ground rule 4): /api/ps unreachable, unload_model failure, unknown model size, ledger lock timeout → emit() a specific banner and proceed with today's plain-generate behavior — the request must still complete; nothing fails silently and nothing beyond the banner blocks the turn.

Tests: evict-order (LRU among unpinned; pinned survive; alternating two models under a one-slot budget still completes both, i.e. thrash is correct-but-bounded behavior); ledger flock test (two processes interleaving read-modify-write lose no update); keep_alive body assertion via injected fake urlopen (localmodels' inject-fake-runners idiom); reconcile-with-ps and corrupt-ledger-rebuild tests.

Multi-model overnight simulation (the plan's gate): scripted fake Ollama server + 11 section profiles issuing interleaved run_local calls across ≥3 distinct models under a budget that fits only 2 — assert the resident set never exceeds budget (per the fake server's load/unload log), all requests complete, pinned models are never unloaded, and the run emits zero unexplained banners.

orchestrator.py:962 (run_local), :971 (request body — keep_alive lands here), :924/:941–950 (run_ollama CLI path + warn-once noop precedent), :374 (acquire_app_lock flock precedent)

tasks.title: Apply-situation resolution: situation ref → required slots, phase filtering, live mid-run switch
tasks.goal: A project's situation ref resolves into the goal manifest's required slots; a phase runs iff its doc_sections intersect the required slots OR it is structurally required (reusing the completeness-profile machinery); changing the Situation mid-run lets running phases finish, recomputes the gap report, and re-evaluates queued routes against the new goal — no new engine, the pull-based Conductor readjusts.
tasks.context: The architectural insight to preserve (sections plan §14.1): the gap report IS the work queue, so applying a Situation is data flowing into existing machinery — the Situation's doc_slots become the goal manifest's required slots (7.5's goal_manifest.json), 5.4's gap scan only demands those slots, and only owning sections/phases run. Phase filtering REUSES completeness.filter_phases (completeness.py:92) — extend it (or add a sibling filter_phases_by_slots) keeping its defensive guarantees verbatim: final phase always kept, a filter that keeps < _MIN_KEPT_PHASES (completeness.py:80) falls back to ALL phases with on_warn, structurally-required phases (build/verification gates) always retained. The project's ref rides run_config.json beside 'completeness' (load_run_config, completeness.py:147) — e.g. {'situation': 'prototype_sprint'}. Mid-run switch semantics live in conductor.py's cycle (7.1/7.5 — VERIFY landed shape; conductor.py does not exist in the repo today): re-read the ref each cycle; running sessions are never killed; queued/deferred routes re-evaluate against the new required slots; the ledger records the switch. CRITICAL: cfg["_ keys are FORBIDDEN for new state (2.3's CI grep gate) — any new per-turn/per-phase state (e.g. the active situation's slot set) rides TurnContext fields or explicit function parameters, never a mutated cfg key.
subtasks: Read the landed 7.5 goal_manifest.json schema and 5.4 gap-artifact schema; record divergences from this card before wiring (trust code over plan).
situations.py: resolve_required_slots(situation, doc_map) -> ordered slot set + owning-section set (via doc_map owner_section from 5.3); pure function, unit-testable without the engine.

completeness.py: add slot-based phase filtering reusing filter_phases' guarantees — a phase is kept iff (a) its section owns ≥1 required slot / its doc_sections intersect, or (b) it is structurally required (final phase, build/verify gates); same _MIN_KEPT_PHASES fallback + on_warn on a gutting filter.

orchestrator.py: read the situation ref from run_config.json (beside 'completeness', load_run_config completeness.py:147); pass the resolved slot set into phase selection via parameters/TurnContext — grep gate: zero new cfg["_ writes.

conductor.py: on each cycle re-read the project's situation ref; on change: ledger a situation_changed entry, install the new required slots into the goal manifest evaluation, let running sessions finish untouched, recompute the gap scan (5.4), and re-evaluate queued/deferred routes — routes targeting slots no longer required are cancelled WITH a ledger reason, never silently dropped.
Unknown/corrupt situation ref: visible banner event + safe default = no slot filtering (all slots required), matching completeness.py's fail-open philosophy — never a silently gutted run.

tests: phase-filter matrix (the plan's gate) — situations × workflows grid asserting exactly which phases run, including the structurally-required and gutting-fallback rows; live-switch test — scripted conductor cycles with a mid-run ref change asserting running-finish/recompute/re-evaluate; grep-gate stays green.

tasks.context: Composition card: build almost nothing new — embed 9.2's DocumentBuilderView and 7.11's PipelineBuilderView as two halves of one editor (sections plan §14.5's 'Situation editor'), plus an overrides tab and the apply flow. Apply flow: compute BEFORE = the project's current effective phase set (its present situation ref or none, via 9.1's engine path), AFTER = the candidate Situation's set; the diff (phases added/removed, sections activated/deactivated, slot-count delta) renders in a confirm sheet; only on confirm does the GUI write run_config.json's situation ref (+ any project-scope override files) — cancel writes NOTHING. The diff must come from the same engine computation as 9.1 (parity-fixture-pinned like 9.2's preview) so the confirm sheet can never lie about what will change. conductor.py side: applying while the Conductor runs relies on 9.1's mid-run switch semantics — the GUI only writes files; it never reaches into the conductor process. tasks.title: /model-effort advisor + /gen-prompt structurer: advisory cards that never run the input
tasks.goal: The two seeded meta commands: /model-effort <prompt> renders an advisor card (recommended model + effort + one-line rationale + estimated cost + 'Run with this' button) from a rubric distilled from the engineering plan's §11 guidance plus live 6.1 capability and 6.4 cost descriptors; /gen-prompt <rough text> renders an editable structured-prompt card (goal, context, constraints, output format, acceptance criteria) inserted into the composer only on confirm — neither command ever executes the input.
tasks.context: Both ride 9.5's meta executor (one cheap call_agent turn, local-preferred). The advisor rubric is DATA, not prose in code: a rubric file distilled from orchestrator-v3-engineering-plan.md §11 ('Model & effort guidance' — fable@max for correctness-catastrophic, xhigh for cross-cutting engine, high default, sonnet for config/JSON plumbing, haiku not recommended) combined at render time with live facts: 6.1's capability descriptors (resolve_capabilities — effort_control per backend; a recommendation may never name an effort the backend lacks) and 6.4's costs.py PRICES (integer micro-USD; unknown model → cost shown as 'unmetered', NEVER an invented estimate — 6.4's honesty rules apply to estimates too: label them '≈' and derive only from known prices + prompt length). 'Run with this' sends the ORIGINAL user prompt with the recommended model/effort applied via the existing per-phase routing vocabulary — a second explicit user action, never automatic. /gen-prompt's card is editable in place; Insert replaces the composer text; Cancel discards; nothing is ever sent by the command itself. Card rendering reuses 4.9's in-stream artifact-card mechanics (fenced card payload in the transcript, GUI renders). The load-bearing invariant, tested with a mocked call_agent: the input prompt string is never passed to any execution path — only quoted inside the single advisory turn. acceptance_criteria: Per-command dispatch (the plan's gate): each of the 15 commands calls exactly its mapped existing verb — proven per-command with mocks; no command reimplements verb logic, and removing a command from commands.json removes it cleanly.

Barrier semantics are honest: /vote, /consensus, and /mode announce that they take effect at the next round barrier and then actually do — the transcript never claims an immediate effect that didn't happen (R2).

/compare renders ONE card with N columns for one prompt; a failing model shows an explicit error cell while the others render; all-fail renders an honest all-failed card; the live debate's roster, session state, and transcript flow are untouched by a compare (verified by golden-adjacent assertion on a session that runs /compare).
/cost shows 6.4's session rollup with full honesty semantics — '≥ $X.XX · N turns unmetered' for mixed sessions, never $0.00 for unmetered; /status reflects the store's real run state.
/help is generated from the merged registry (fleet→section→project) — a project-added command appears; a deleted one disappears.

The popover is fully keyboard-driven (arrows/Enter/Esc), ranks via the shared fuzzyScore, shows kind badges, and never steals the composer's text; it is visually and behaviorally distinct from ⌘K (§3.5 — shared idioms, separate surface).
Commands that mutate the room (/cast, /mode, /vote, /consensus) produce visible transcript announcements; nothing changes silently (§6.2/R2).

QA verifies: 15-command dispatch matrix green, /compare failure-cell tests green, popover keyboard tests green, StyleGuard (the plan's gate) green, golden suite byte-green for command-free sessions, make verify green; manual: /audit round-trips through QA (epic exit-gate item).
